## Current 1.0 execution and evidence

`CircuitRun` uses JAX CPU in the calling Python process. Its constructor has no
`backend` keyword; Python 3.12 and the base package supply the runtime. Josephson
junction and SQUID branches retain their declared linear small-signal meaning.
HB and external Julia execution are retired from 1.0.

| Choice | Ownership |
|---|---|
| `storage="memory"` | Detached values and actual same-call numerical evidence; no Workspace or saved identity |
| `workspace=path` | Immutable SQLite evidence v3, internal store revision 8, fixed completion and readonly resolve |
| `prepare` / `warmup` | Detached numerical callable / compile-only preparation; no baseline solve |
| `close` | Release Run-owned resources; returned values and fixed saved selections remain readable |

Direct and parameter-swept Direct stream the same call's host arrays to checked
binary objects without an operation spool. Optimization retains its spool and
lazy stage history. Completed chunks alone do not select success; final
manifest/result/completion/attempt/success publication is atomic.
Each public `stage.history` contains its own saved baseline, when present,
before ordered evaluations. This adds no evaluation or iteration and changes
no optimizer counter. Stage/model/kind/ordinal and source ancestry remain bound.

Direct and Operator Results, including each Sweep point, expose readonly
same-call evidence in Memory, Workspace and resolve. Conditional affine evidence
is absent when unused; when used it records the actual candidate, affected edges
and authorization source. Evidence does not rerun numerical work.

[Workspace evidence v3](contracts/workspace-evidence-v3.qmd) defines exact
binary fields and version domains. Plan/Request/ParameterSet canonical document
versions remain unchanged. Old evidence is rejected read-only before directory,
lock or SQLite mutation, then checked again under the ordinary lock. The error
explicitly identifies a pre-1.0 development build that 1.0 does not support;
use a new Workspace and recompute. There is no old-format reader or migration.

The reader-facing [Simulation conventions](concepts/simulation-conventions.qmd)
connect these version-bound rules to the canonical phasor, wave-reference, and
linewidth definitions without adding a second runtime contract.

## JAX physical program {#physical-program-target}

This contract remains **CONVERGING**. The shared JAX physical program retains
the existing physical equations and checked numerical authority. One physical program maps ordered
real scalar parameter coordinates to physical quantities. Direct evaluation,
sweeps, dependency queries, Sensitivity and Optimization consume that same
program, including parameter-dependent View weights, loads and reference
impedances. Existing units, phasor signs, physical equations, ordinary transpose
and numerical certification conditions remain in force. Schematic work remains
incomplete and deferred.

### Checked JAX memory ownership {#jax-memory-completion}

The authorized CONVERGING target extends the existing memory Direct and
Optimization flows to checked JAX `evaluate`, Sensitivity and declared
ParameterSpace/Sweep. Storage selection changes result ownership and publication,
not physical equations, branch certification, units, declaration order or
failure semantics. The same prepared request and physical numerical producer
feed either a RAM result sink or Workspace publication. No second evaluator,
unchecked replacement, fabricated saved identity or disk-spill path is admitted.

The RAM sink owns actual synchronized output arrays and typed numerical evidence.
Point and Sweep Results retain declared parameter/frequency order, realized
mesh/View/loading, units and actual failure information. Sensitivity retains
ordered primal values, requested derivative blocks, partial availability and
one shared equation-evidence authority. Detached immutable Results and existing
selected presentation/report consumers remain usable after Run close without
hidden numerical execution. Run keeps only the last compact operation Benchmark;
its compile owner remains bounded and operation-local factors/AD frames drain
before a Result is returned. Full requested output/history retention is explicit
RAM ownership, not a disk cache or permission to silently discard results.
Memory Sweep selectors retain a detached binding from the same captured Plan
alias table and prepared View. Public ElectricNodeRef and scoped CoordinateRef
handles, canonical IDs and derived View coordinates use the existing pure
selector encoder; foreign-Plan handles and ambiguous aliases retain their
existing failure semantics. No Run, Plan, saved decoder/reader closure or live
capture is stored in the Result. Filtered selections preserve original source
indices and order rather than inventing new point identities.

Saved `resolve`, durable checkpoint and crash resume remain Workspace
responsibilities. Memory analysis and Sensitivity use their real checked producer/Result
consumer handoffs; unsupported saved recovery still fails before
numerical work. Such a capability error is not a root-finding failure. Compile-only warmup uses the same actual variants and bounded declared
preparation-point traversal, without root/baseline evaluation or invented frame
consumer signatures.

RF root localization is a separate numerical scope. A caller-declared search
region and selection policy must be explicit and separate from the existing
Hint/anchor. No default multiplied frequency range or new tolerance is inferred.
Opening memory storage cannot itself change the root residual, locate a branch
or establish that an RF root is absent. Original observations and the inactive
root-policy proposal retain their original identities and limits.

### Workspace and checked memory ownership {#memory-direct-storage}

`CircuitRun(plan=plan, storage="workspace", workspace=path)` retains the saved
default: binding, recovery, fixed saved Results and readonly resolution.
`CircuitRun(plan=plan, storage="memory")` omits Workspace
binding entirely. Supplying a Workspace or enabling `versioned` with memory
storage is invalid. Construction, preparation, warmup, solve and cleanup in
this mode create no SCNSim Workspace, SQLite record, filesystem operation lease,
scratch/spool, object/index, checkpoint or timing publication.

Memory point Direct retains its existing dedicated typed response adapter.
Declared Direct ParameterSpace and checked evaluate point/Sweep consume the
same ordinary numerical producer through a RAM sink; checked Sensitivity uses
the same primal/derivative producer. View operations, declaration dependencies,
detached `prepare` and compile-only `warmup` remain available. Warmup and
execution use the same physical variants, precision and bounded Run compile
owner as the Workspace path. Numerical equations, selected loading, sparse
certificates and native failures remain authoritative; memory storage is not
an unchecked solver or different physics implementation. Memory Optimization
retains the existing shared strategy coordinator. Workspace recovery
and saved-result `resolve` remain outside the memory scope and fail before
storage or numerical work.

Point Direct `solve` returns `InMemoryDirectSolveResult`, a `Result` with detached immutable
S/Y/Z matrices, trace leaves, units, View/loading and discretization metadata.
It is not a receipt-backed `AnalysisResult` and has no fabricated saved
`ResultIdentity`, attempt, completion or persistence authority. Existing matrix
and trace presentation applies to its actual returned arrays; those arrays
remain caller-owned after `Run.close()`.

Memory timing supports `timing="aggregate"` only; detailed timing is rejected
before numerical work. Saved aggregate/detailed behavior is unchanged.

`result.benchmark` is an immutable `InMemoryBenchmarkResult` for that call.
The memory Run keeps only its last compact operation Benchmark, available via
`run.benchmark()`; it never keeps an output/history ledger. Before the first
operation it raises `ResultUnavailableError`; memory Benchmark accepts no
filters, since there is no operation history to select. Timing may be
collected in memory, with unavailable clocks explicit, but is never written
to a Workspace. Run activity spans preparation, synchronized compute, result
assembly and cleanup, so an active call still rejects `close`. Closing releases
Run warm references, not the caller's returned arrays or Benchmark. Memory
allocation or compilation failures remain real errors; there is no disk-spill
fallback or automatic switch to saved storage.

This storage option is **CONVERGING**. The current published dev28 source and
its observations retain their original identities. Source implementation alone
does not establish current 10001-point memory timing or a Julia performance
comparison.

| Surface | Current responsibility |
|---|---|
| `run.dependencies(quantities=...)` | Declared direct and indirect physical dependencies; no execution or proof of globally nonzero derivatives |
| `run.sensitivity(SensitivitySpec(...), parameters=...)` | Ordered primal values and requested `Jacobian`, `JVP` or `VJP`, with separate primal and derivative status |
| `run.optimize(OptimizationSpec(...))` | CMA-ES, genuine L-BFGS-B, projected L-BFGS and ordered Hybrid stages share the quantity/objective evaluator |
| `run.resolve(..., attempt={'attempt_id': recorded_attempt_id})` | Explicit readonly terminal partial Sensitivity selection; partial evidence is excluded from complete-success caches and default resolution |

Complex outputs have explicit real/imaginary coordinates. Jacobian entry
$(i,j)$ has units $q_i/\theta_j$, with ordered input/output axes. Explicit scales
and optimizer coordinate chain rules are recorded separately from physical
derivatives. Only the requested derivative mode is stored; reading JVP/VJP
never executes a missing full Jacobian.

The CONVERGING dev37 presentation candidate lets a Sensitivity Result's
`plot()` and `show()` methods select already-saved named quantities in caller
order. Within each quantity, rows retain the saved coordinate order and columns
retain authored `wrt` order. Selection is mutually exclusive with the existing
`block_id` route; JVP/VJP remain block-selected, and `show()` without an
operation kind remains the summary view. Compatible derivative-unit groups
share one figure with separate panels; nonmember cells and unavailable
derivatives remain distinguishable from numeric zero. It is a display
projection: it does not recompute, mutate or change Result ownership. The
[Sensitivity guide](guides/sensitivity.qmd) defines the selected-unit and
figure behavior.

Each output expression uses its own ordered leaf mapping into the shared
physical frame. Repeated leaves, mixed Views and real/imaginary projections
retain the declared occurrence and unit; a local leaf ordinal is not a global
observable index. Primal and derivative public projection share this mapping.

### Memory Optimization ownership {#memory-optimization-storage}

The CONVERGING candidate extends the same
`CircuitRun(plan=plan, storage="memory")` and `run.optimize(...)` interface to
existing CMA, L-BFGS-B and declared Hybrid strategies. It uses the same physical
Objective/root authority, fixed stage models, original-point branch anchors,
ordered candidate work and real gradient projection. Memory integration is implemented as a CONVERGING candidate. The distinct `ProjectedLBFGSSpec` declares projected L-BFGS with value-first
rejection of failed trials. This is the implementation choice for the authorized
reject-and-continue behavior, not a Human-selected algorithm or accepted
mathematical scope. `LBFGSBSpec` retains genuine SciPy L-BFGS-B semantics.
The new controller is implemented; no failed trial gradient is fabricated.
Current observations remain bound to their exact candidate source; no
improved-search or acceptance claim follows.

`ProjectedLBFGSSpec` has explicit `max_evaluations`, `max_iterations`, `ftol`,
`gtol`, `max_line_search`, `commit_every_iterations` and optional unit-bearing
`coordinate_scales`, matching the existing local control declaration fields.
Its canonical strategy is `projected_lbfgs`, including Hybrid stage and
progress provenance; it is not an alias for `lbfgsb`. Failed trial values and
original failures remain visible while smaller trials may continue. An
unavailable gradient is never replaced with zero, NaN or a stale gradient.
Accepted iterates, original-point baseline/root anchors and fatal-error
responsibility remain shared with the existing physical execution authority.

The candidate controller works in the declared local coordinate map, using
the width of resolved bounds when a bounded variable has neither explicit nor
declared scale. Open linear domains keep their declared scale; signed-log
domains retain their existing reference-based mapping.
It projects directions at active bounds, and retains up to ten accepted-real
secant pairs for its two-loop direction. A non-descent direction uses the actual
negative projected gradient. The direction first establishes a feasible bounded
endpoint and its displacement from the accepted point. The initial unit search
step uses that displacement; unavailable or nondecreasing trials halve the
displacement step within the explicit evaluation and line-search budgets. Acceptance requires a lower actual
cost and its actual gradient. The declared `gtol`, `ftol` and iteration limit
retain their roles; exact zero projected displacement reports technical
stagnation. No Armijo constant, new tolerance, finite-difference gradient or
fabricated trial gradient is introduced. These are candidate algorithm details,
not a universal convergence or global optimum guarantee.

A primal-valid trial whose gradient is unavailable retains its finite cost and
computed components. Its separate `optimizer_unavailability` records the actual
`kind`, `detail`, `role="candidate_value_gradient"` and evidence. A failed primal
trial retains its original numerical failure and +Inf penalty. Ordinary CMA
trials do not require a gradient, so a missing CMA gradient is not itself local
optimizer unavailability. Every attempted failed or rejected point remains in
the caller-owned history; accepted iterates remain separately identifiable.

Omitted checkpoint resolves to `off` for memory and the established
`generation` default for Workspace. Memory rejects an explicit durable
checkpoint, exact saved resume or saved accepted-iterate restart before storage
access. It creates no Workspace, filesystem lease, SQL journal, spool/scratch,
object/index, recovery/checkpoint or timing publication, and has no disk-spill
fallback. Compile-only Optimization warmup binds the same requested stage
variants without root, baseline or factor evaluation.

`InMemoryOptimizationResult` extends `Result`, without a saved
ResultIdentity/attempt/completion or resolve authority. Its detached immutable
projections retain exact parameter points, ordinals, stage/model identity,
original numerical failure kind/stage/reason/evidence, failed-trial +Inf cost,
observed best, actually accepted iterations and comparison facts. Each failed
trial remains visible; failure penalty is not proof of physical infeasibility.
History and accepted rows belong to the returned Result, not to a Run output
ledger. Numeric bodies have one in-memory authority rather than duplicated
per-term evidence. After close the caller can read existing histories and
figures without rerunning a numerical API.

The Run retains only its last compact aggregate InMemoryBenchmarkResult.
Activity spans preparation, compute, callbacks, synchronization/drain, typed
assembly and cleanup. `OptimizationProgress.persistence` defaults to
`"workspace"`; memory events carry `"memory"` and describe RAM-observed/accepted
work with durable committed counts of zero. No RAM publication is called a
saved ACK. Original-kind-before-conversion root continuation, baseline/fatal
responsibility and callback primary errors remain intact. No zero/NaN/stale
gradient, blanket retry or hidden strategy fallback may make an unavailable
local trial appear valid. The rejection-controller integration and actual installed
memory Optimization observations remain separate unfinished items; this scope
has no acceptance or efficacy claim.

### Direct within-chunk stage batching

The existing configurable main frequency bucket (default eight) and stable
size-one tail bound ordinary Direct stage work. Within one chunk, general
point arithmetic is mapped across lanes; each ready bundle crosses the host
boundary once for its independent sparse equations. Each lane still owns its
actual matrix, RHS, local factor and numerical certificate. Different matrices
do not share a factor or become a new physical model.

The physical order for each point remains W, then actual Y/Z/S formation and
its existing checks, then source W. Those two equation stages form separate
ready bundles. Already-ready later lanes may perform work before an earlier
lane's later-stage failure is known. Actual lane performed/presence/status and
evidence remain truthful; both semantic failure reducers retain original
frequency occurrence order. Failure stops new external submissions and drains
work already in flight; unexpected fatal errors retain their cause and cleanup
responsibility. This is not a cross-frequency skip or bitwise-work-equivalence
promise, a retry policy, or a new numerical condition.

Unknown total native scratch still admits one external chunk slot; known
output bytes are not a total estimate. No private four-slot override is a
shipped resource default. Each lane's native factor is released before that native equation call or
bundle returns; a host lane loop need not retain multiple factors at once.
JAX point/chunk arrays remain through synchronization and required consumption,
then are released. CompileOwner retains static programs and executables only. Memory Direct keeps its existing no-persistence contract.
Warmup and execution use the same successor producer callable, abstract
signature, key and source-bound identity. Warmup performs no factorization,
baseline or numerical solve; a producer change requires its actual variant,
not a relabeled previous warm hit. Genuine actual-frame consumers remain lazy
until the same producer's exact static tree is available. Existing observations
retain their source identities; this candidate makes no speed prediction or
cross-platform performance claim. Root/N2 policy and Julia numerical scope are
unchanged.

### Detached callable and scheduling ownership

`run.prepare(quantities=..., parameters=..., wrt=..., discretization=...,
precision=...)` acquires a detached `PreparedFunction` from the same physical
Quantity/View declarations. Omitted `wrt` selects captured continuous parameters
in canonical order. Remaining supplied point values are constants. Its
`numeric_function(theta_SI, omega_rad_per_s, seeds)` returns packed values and
fixed-shape auxiliary status. Immutable layouts bind units, axes, real/imaginary
components, fixed mesh, branch controls and selected dtype. The caller-held
function remains usable after `Run.close()` without retaining Run or Workspace.
Raw outputs have no certified Result or publication authority. High-level checked
Sensitivity retains separate primal and derivative failures; successful primal
auxiliary status cannot hide a failed tangent or adjoint. Native transforms use
the original callable, never an AOT executable. The replacement has no parallel
physical evaluator or generic Python AD interpreter.

`CircuitRun(..., execution_policy=ExecutionPolicy())` supplies optional resource
settings; omission uses the same defaults. ExecutionPolicy is separate from
numerical request identity. Defaults
are eight-frequency chunks, in-flight work resolved from worker capacity,
the optional `max_in_flight` setting and scratch estimates, a 256 MiB scratch target,
and owner-local compile limits of
16 static entries, 16 variants and 256 MiB known bytes. The configured positive
`frequency_chunk_size` selects the main bucket; warmup uses that same bucket
and a stable size-one tail, deduplicated when the main bucket is one.
Unknown per-frequency scratch estimates use one ready slot. The scratch target
also bounds operation-local output batching; neither role promises an OS
residency limit. A legitimate individual item exceeding the scratch target is not
rejected, remeshed or silently recast. One primary parallel axis governs frequency
or candidate work. Estimate-based frequency admission is required by this
candidate contract. Current native factor fill and backend working-set totals
are unknown, so admission uses one slot; known matrix-output bytes are a
diagnostic lower bound, not a total estimate. Actual resource observations
remain bound to their installed candidate. Static entries and prepared handles are pinned through actual
synchronization; finite owner-local eviction releases unused entries. All-pinned
overflow remains operation-owned. Unknown byte counts remain unknown; no global
cache purge is performed. `run.warmup(prepared, transforms=("value", "jvp", "vjp"))` and the existing
`run.warmup(view, spec, parameters=...)` form use the same preparation authority,
report prepared versus lazy signatures, and do not solve or publish success.
Raw aggregate transforms and high-level candidate/frequency-chunk variants are
distinct compiled signatures. A raw aggregate compile does not establish a
chunk warm hit: reuse requires the same provider callable/key, shape, dtype,
device and fixed capability partition. Known main/tail chunks and declared root/coupling value signatures are
reported separately. Root packet shapes come from abstract evaluation, and
compilation does not run Newton or sparse solves. Unrequested derivative or
future signatures stay lazy. Known checked candidate/joint-branch linearization
producers may also prepare for Sensitivity or explicit derivative transforms.
Their frame consumers remain lazy until the SAME cached producer supplies its
exact Partial static metadata; matching array shapes alone do not establish
reuse. Sensitivity warmup binds its finalized leaf Views, point, active
coordinates and discretization through the existing Sensitivity producer.
Explicit `batch_shapes` are leading theta point-batch dimensions. Warmup
reports compile time, reuse, admission and cache counts; generated code bytes
do not establish total executable residency, which remains unknown. Native
transform and resource observations remain pending for this candidate.

### Fixed discretization and derivative boundaries

The checked Sensitivity host chooses forward Jacobian columns when the active
input count does not exceed the packed real output count, otherwise reverse
rows. It reuses one linearization or pullback and maps directions in blocks of
eight; this is an execution strategy, not a scientific size limit. Explicit JVP
and VJP keep their requested direction or cotangent and do not materialize a
missing full Jacobian. Sparse, dense and paired equation primitives carry actual
primal/tangent/mixed/adjoint role, derivative order, occurrence dependency and
performed certificate facts. A successful primal certificate does not certify
an unavailable or failed derivative equation.
Mapped roots execute scalar primal control sequentially under the pinned JAX
checkify boundary, preserving Newton early exit, status and iteration policy.
The scalar checked Error and packet cross that mapping together; owned checks
are reintroduced outside its opaque call rather than replaced by status alone.
The finite archive bridge retains owned equation site/role/order/dependency and
mapped-lane presence/code payloads while exposing scalar first-failure control.
Raw callers do not acquire high-level certification from that debug bridge.
Their implicit derivative remains the closed local equation; this mapping is
not a promise of parallel root searches or reverse AD through Newton history.
Blocked directions carry ordered check payloads associated with their actual
basis column or output row; the outer primal check remains separate. Successful
Sensitivity publication seals one shared equation-evidence body in the same
completion transaction. Quantities reference that body rather than duplicating
its certificates. Unavailable reasons are compact descriptors, not retained
check objects or numerical frames.

High-level response derivatives use bounded residual state for the selected
chunk. Reverse composition across frequencies may require explicit bounded
replay of chunk work after a compact output projection; this is not a promise
of zero recomputation or a whole-response retained tape. A caller-held raw
PreparedFunction has different ownership: JAX transformations may retain their
own residuals, which remain the caller's responsibility rather than a certified
high-level resource or Result guarantee.

A Sensitivity point or any optimization stage, including CMA-ES, binds realized sections, sparse pattern, matrix shapes,
coordinate order and retained/eliminated partition. Finite declared length
bounds may support conservative section planning where actual material
dependence permits it. Missing finite bounds warn, without an invented maximum
range, adequacy claim or new eligibility condition. Stages freeze realized
section counts; at fixed $N$, $\Delta x=\ell/N$ remains parameter dependent.
ElectricalResolution retains its lossless planning domain; an explicitly fixed-count
lossy model is separate. Active L/C dependencies require a justified bound;
otherwise planning warns and fixes the starting realized mesh without claiming
adequacy. Dynamic coarse exploration is limited to non-Optimization requests.
These are derivatives of a discrete physical model, not continuum or global
optimum guarantees. Remeshing requires a new explicit stage/request,
reevaluation and empty local curvature history, not a line-search shape change.

Scalar/affine physical mappings remain traced through lowering. An identically
zero resistance specialization requires a structurally zero declared dependency;
an active resistance currently equal to zero retains its derivative. Explicit
scalar-to-fixed-shape RLGC mappings are separate from whole-RLGC values, with
no implicit promotion of matrix entries to independent parameters.

Sparse derivatives follow $A\,dx=db-dA\,x$. Physical ordinary transpose differs
from the adjoint of explicit real coordinates. Root derivatives follow the
same certified primal branch, including vector, gauge, slope, residue and mixed
frequency/parameter dependencies. Degeneracy, gauge singularity and nonsmoothness
report derivative unavailability, not invented zero gradients or automatic
finite-difference fallbacks. A derivative failure does not relabel a successful
primal value. No new tolerance, precision fallback or mean-root policy is added.

### Optimizer, evidence and resource ownership

CMA-ES retains complete post-tell state and exact resume responsibility.
`commit_every_generations` applies only to CMA stages. Each `LBFGSBSpec`
requires `commit_every_iterations` for committed accepted iterates; trial or
tangent evaluations do not become recovery checkpoints or durable callbacks.
Local accepted-iterate evidence supports a fresh restart, not a CMA/RNG or
curvature checkpoint.
L-BFGS-B uses explicit scaled physical coordinates and bounds; restart begins a
new stage from a committed accepted iterate with empty curvature history, not
exact solver resume. `LBFGSBSpec` requires explicit `max_evaluations`,
`max_iterations`, `ftol`, `gtol`, `max_line_search` and
`commit_every_iterations`. Supplied coordinate scales bind every local variable
in its physical unit. For a linear mapping, explicit scale takes precedence over
the declared domain scale: $\theta=\theta_0+s x$. A bounded variable with
neither uses the width of its resolved physical bounds; open linear domains
retain their declared scale. A declared log mapping uses
$\theta=\theta_0\exp(a x)$, where $a=s/|\theta_0|$ when a scale applies and
$a=1$ for an unscaled signed-log domain. The actual nonzero starting reference
retains the sign for signed log domains; finite log bounds retain their declared
positive physical bounds. The chain rule is $d\theta/dx=s$ for affine
coordinates and $a\theta$ for log coordinates. Each map records
reference, scale/source, exponent scale, units and native transformed bounds;
there is no CMA folding, clipping, invented open-domain interval or epsilon.
Bounds/domain/transform and full effective initial parameters remain recorded
separately. Trial points are not accepted checkpoints. Hybrid stages
record observed winner, accepted iterate, termination, budget, seed, mesh and
transition. Each encoded stage owns resolved controller settings, the effective
seed declaration and its explicit mesh override or shared planning declaration.
A null first-stage seed uses the operation's effective starting point. A null
later-stage seed consumes the recorded selected physical point and reevaluates
it under the target model before that stage starts. An explicit seed override
records the full merged effective point. Future selected points and their CMA
coordinates are not fabricated in the initial request.
Top-level best is absent until a full cost is actually evaluated
under the final comparison model; stage winners remain separate. A transition records the actual source candidate/model, seed selection, target
model and target reevaluation locator. These references are bound atomically
with the first target-stage batch; there is no standalone transition commit. A partial terminal attempt
remains partial even when it records an observed best point.
A derivative-unavailable local stage stops there and seals a PARTIAL Hybrid
terminal; later declared stages remain unentered. There is no automatic bypass
or strategy fallback. Preserved accepted/observed physical points may seed an
explicit new stage/restart. Final-comparison best remains nullable when the
comparison stage has not been entered. That comparison's baseline is the
original operation effective point, actually reevaluated under the declared
comparison model; a later stage's selected-point seed is not this baseline.
Comparison preparation evaluations/counts/cost are recorded separately from
the optimizer controller search budget and SciPy `nfev`.

`checkpoint="off"` suppresses physical recovery checkpoints/pointers and
dedicated CMA/RNG/anchor restore state; it preserves numerical stage and
accepted-point facts. An explicit local restart from a committed accepted point
starts a new stage with cleared curvature, distinct from exact CMA resume.
A later CMA stage constructs its mean from the actual selected physical seed
using the same declared unit-box/domain map; it does not mutate deferred seed
coordinates in the sealed operation request.

`OptimizationProgress` records `stage_id` and `strategy` (`cmaes` or `lbfgsb`).
CMA uses completed/total/committed generation counters; local stages use
completed/total/committed iteration counters. Nonapplicable or unavailable
counters are `None`, and best cost may be absent before the final comparison.
The phase vocabulary includes `iteration`, `stage_transition` and `partial`
in addition to existing initial/resume/generation/complete/result-reuse phases.
Durable callbacks follow actual ACK, without publishing trial evaluations.
Budget and evaluation fields describe the named current stage:
`requested_budget` is its declared `max_evaluations`. CMA's
`achievable_evaluations` retains its baseline plus complete-population count;
local adaptive stages record `None`. `evaluated_count` is the stage's controller
observation, not a count of physical cache misses or a substitute for recorded
SciPy evaluation/iteration counters. Hybrid does not invent a summed achievable
budget from these fields.

SQLite operation evidence uses internal revision **8** and evidence **v3**. Fixed readers select verified stored blocks and
minimum metadata without retaining Run, AD tape, factor or live connection,
and without recomputing missing derivatives. Old operation Workspaces require
recomputation, with no compatibility reader.

JAX is the sole numerical runtime. Pure callbacks have fixed-shape
value/status handoffs and no Workspace, progress or mutable global factor/cache
side effects. Operation-local owners retain primal, tangent and adjoint work
until it returns and synchronizes before lease release or native-limit
restoration. Explicit Run warm holders, fixed-stage programs and call-local numerical work
have separate ownership.
Factor reuse describes actual controlled calls, not a factor-once promise.
Timing, sampled memory, source and execution identity are distinct evidence;
Checked derivative entry points support explicit JVP/VJP and required frequency
jets; arbitrary raw `jax.grad` through host branch selection is not promised.
AD gives no speed, memory, bitwise or achieved-accuracy bound.

The public declarations are `SensitivitySpec`, `Jacobian`, `JVP`, `VJP`,
`OutputCoordinate`, `SensitivityScales`, `FixedMeshSpec`, `LBFGSBSpec`,
`OptimizationStage`, `HybridSpec` and `AcceptedIterateSelection`. Matrix quantities
use `DirectSolveSpec.S`, `.Y`, `.Z` or `OperatorSpec.matrix`, with `.on(view)` on
each leaf, including mixed-View expressions. Sensitivity requires explicit
leaf `.on(view)` bindings from the same Run and has no public default View.
`run.optimize(view, spec)` supplies the default only to unbound objective leaves;
explicit leaf Views retain their own identity. `run.optimize(spec)` requires
all leaves to be bound. The compiler's `default_view` argument is that explicit
lowering handoff, not an automatic original-View selection.
`normalized_jacobian` is a stored
Result projection using request-recorded scales, not a second differentiation
call. JVP directions have each parameter's physical unit and a dimensionless
path coordinate. VJP weights times output coordinates share a declared scalar
functional unit; input cotangents have functional-unit/parameter-unit dimensions.
Zero weights still carry explicit units. `OutputCoordinate.index` contains only
physical array-axis ordinals, with `()` for a scalar; `component` is separate.
Rows flatten physical axes in C order with real/imag components last and
fastest; real outputs have only the real component. Algorithm termination controls and
reasons are not design acceptance conditions.

`ScalarRLGCMap(base, terms=...)` uses `RLGCScalarTerm(source, resistance=...,
inductance=..., conductance=..., capacitance=...)`; source is a scalar
`ParameterRef` or `AffineMap`. Each basis matrix has the per-length field unit
divided by the source's physical unit. Individual bases need not be passive or
positive definite; the realized total uses the existing RLGC physical validator
at every point, retaining conductor order, reference and base provenance.

The [parameter contract](contracts/parameter-system.qmd#parameterized-rlgc-scope),
[architecture](implementation/system-architecture.qmd) and
[backend guide](implementation/benchmark-and-backends.qmd) and
[Sensitivity usage guide](guides/sensitivity.qmd) retain their own
implementation responsibilities without a parallel physical-program contract.

## Package ownership and lifecycle {#package-lifecycle}

The dev27 **CONVERGING source candidate** retains the ownership and lazy
Result boundary established in dev24 and uses SQLite operation evidence revision 8.
The physical-program section above owns the new derivative and optimizer
semantics; this section owns lifecycle and storage responsibilities.
Historical observations retain their original version and scope; they are not
observations of this candidate. Schematic completion remains incomplete and deferred.

### Run and operation ownership

`CircuitRun` remains the public facade for `solve`, `evaluate`, `optimize`,
`resolve`, `warmup`, `explain`, inventory and reports. Parameter binding, request
encoding, preparation, execution, Workspace access and decoding have separate
owners; a mutable Run is not their common context. Compiled models and realized
Views are immutable handoffs independent of a Workspace.

| Owner | Held state | Release boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Process | PJRT initialization and runtime resource configuration | Process exit; closing a Run does not reset them |
| Plan | Authoring capture and sealing | Plan lifetime; Run close does not unseal |
| Run | Fixed binding, necessary lookup and explicitly admitted static physical programs/prepared executables | Optional close or disappearance of its references |
| Operation | Backend, workers, resource authorization, spool and diagnostics | Success, failure or interruption after necessary cleanup |
| Optimization stage | Fixed-model physical program and prepared variants | Stage/operation completion and cleanup; no implicit Run admission |
| Candidate/ready wave | Call-local inputs, frames, factors, outcomes and prepared packets; cache retains lightweight spool references | Ordered consumption and required publication; no full numerical history retained |
| Continuation step | Temporary compiler, material, View, pattern, factor and executable references | Synchronized evaluation and observation, before recursion |
| Result | Fixed evidence root, minimum immutable metadata and delivered values | Caller ownership; no Run or execution-resource capture |
| Workspace | Committed bodies, occurrences, checkpoints and diagnostics | Explicit data management, never Run close |

Normal operation cleanup does not require `run.close()` or a public context
manager. Optional `close()` is idempotent and releases only Run-owned resources.
Operation registration and close share one short lifecycle lock: OPEN is checked
and active work registered atomically; registration includes preparation,
execution, commit, callback, decoding and cleanup. Close with active work raises
the existing state error and does not cancel it. Once CLOSED, new operations are
rejected even if cleanup fails. Blocking cleanup and user callbacks run outside
that lock. Original errors retain priority over cleanup errors.

External Views may keep their Run alive. Internal Run-owned View declarations
must not create a strong Run→View→Run cycle. Results, decoder closures and lazy
readers do not retain a Run. Explicit warm holders differ from operation-local
executables; a weak shared index does not own their lifetime. Reference release
does not promise immediate allocator, mapped-memory or RSS return.

### Operation lease, storage and recovery

An operation obtains a stable OS lease before scratch or native resource
creation, and retains it through publication and cleanup. Its inode/descriptor
is distinct from short Workspace locks and SQL transactions. Supervisor handoff
is explicit; PID and age alone never establish that cleanup is safe. Numerical
work and callbacks do not execute inside SQL transactions or storage locks.

JAX and native execution also hold a private same-request execution lease, preserving
cache selection and one-success publication while short storage locks are
released for child work. It is distinct from root/operation activity leases.
For native work, the supervisor additionally retains its descriptor through actual drain; this is not
a new public concurrency mode or a change to native numerical bodies.

SQLite operation evidence revision 8 retains one canonical scientific body, separate task-local occurrences and
restore state. Numerical evidence and required indexes become visible at the
same atomic publication boundary. Only complete CMA post-tell generations support exact controller resume;
local committed accepted iterates support fresh restart. Baseline is not
generation zero. Durable callbacks follow ACK;
uncertain commits use transaction-identity reconciliation, not blind resubmission.
Timing and instant progress remain separate from numerical success/checkpoints.

Creating a Run performs bounded transaction recovery and lease-aware cleanup of
its centralized abandoned operation scratch. It verifies schema, binding and
necessary commit state, without scanning all historical bodies or directories.
`recover_workspace()` shares this implementation and never resumes computation.
Full database/body/history audit is explicit maintenance, not routine opening.
Pure readonly access does not recover, delete or solve. Unsupported old operation
Workspaces require a new Workspace and recomputation: no compatible reader,
migration or automatic destructive rebuild. Preserved Julia native artifacts
retain their backend-specific format responsibility.

### Fixed, detached and lazy Results

A completed Result fixes Workspace/leaf instance, Plan, request, attempt,
completion seal, selected generation ancestry, baseline/best, history length and
reference-directory root. It never reselects latest success or follows a replaced
leaf. Fixing this root does not preload every candidate reference.

`ResultIdentity.attempt_sha256` continues to name the canonical completed
terminal attempt document, not the initial running-attempt allocation. The
SQLite completion seal includes `terminal_attempt_ref` so this identity can be
verified without replaying task history. SQLite revision 8 does not renumber the Plan,
request or authoring snapshot schemas.

`OptimizationResult.ledger` is a readonly generation Sequence; indexing and
Python negative-index/slice semantics decode only selected generations into
detached immutable values. `len()` uses the fixed length. Flat
`candidate_discretization` uses the same fixed candidate locators. Complete
iteration or `ledger[:]` is explicit caller materialization. Each read acquires a
short readonly snapshot, verifies its selected seal/body and releases before
return or iterator yield. Missing, corrupt or replaced evidence fails plainly,
without selecting another attempt or replaying whole task history. Unread bodies
are not claimed verified. Accessors do not accumulate all previously read bodies;
caller-held point outcomes may retain their own loaded values. Run close does not
invalidate Result access; deleting Workspace invalidates unread portions, while
already delivered detached values remain usable.

History/objective/parameter plots consume bound summary projections; comparison
consumes baseline and exact best; detail tables consume selected candidate bodies.
Plot/show/repr/Notebook display must not first materialize full dependency history.
Indexes and summaries are bound to the same completion seal, not a second
numerical authority. Benchmark consumes only operation diagnostics and necessary
result references, and never launches an experiment or solver.

### Native supervision

::: {.callout-note}

## Contract scope

After reading this contract, a package consumer should understand:

1. how explicit components, wiring, ownership, and public boundaries produce
   the one physical Plan;
2. why an ASCDLS Plan projection and an independently selected analysis View
   serve different jobs;
3. how one Plan produces several lazy reduction references;
4. which calls execute work and which calls only resolve sealed evidence;
5. how every physical value carries a checked unit;
6. how a target parameter point or ordered space binds the Plan without
   changing its topology;
7. which topology, coordinate, and boundary operations SCNSim applies to one
   declared circuit;
8. how Direct matrix responses and typed physical quantities share one
   evaluation contract;
9. how one HB request represents DC, AC, multi-tone, and mixed operating
   cases; and
10. which identities and artifacts make a result reproducible across Python
   processes.

This document defines public product/runtime behavior. Circuit physics,
scientific Gates, and consumer Design Targets remain in their own authorized
sources.

The model-first [Engineer course](index.qmd) teaches these objects in short Lessons
grouped into complete clean-kernel Chapters. The
Concept pages explain the design pressures behind
[circuit models, subsystems, and reuse](concepts/physical-authority-and-reusable-composition.qmd),
[network views](concepts/compilation-coordinates-and-network-views.qmd),
[execution and Result ownership](concepts/requests-execution-and-result-ownership.qmd),
[Direct realization](concepts/direct-and-hb-realizations.qmd), and
[optimization](concepts/units-parameters-and-optimization.qmd). This Contract
remains the exact authority for signatures, formulas, invariants, failures,
receipt evidence, and limits. The separate
[Implementation Design](contracts/index.qmd#implementation-design) explains how
the Runtime realizes this public behavior without becoming a second public
contract.

## Product and lifecycle boundary

SCNSim owns:

- Python circuit authoring and runtime interfaces;
- reusable component Libraries and typed presentation surfaces;
- physical node-flux compilation and Direct C/K/G;
- coordinate transforms and Schur-complement reduction;
- Direct and harmonic-balance analysis;
- Direct optimization, immutable receipts, results, and reports; and
- authoring and compiler-expanded schematic projections of the original
  circuit plan.

SCNSim does not own:

- consumer Design Targets, optimization Gates, or consumer application
  notebook source;
- private consumer values, layouts, manifests, artifacts, or evidence;
- SCGSim layout/EM execution or OrPen PDK source;
- JosephsonCircuits as a library;
- quantization; or
- the legacy Circuit Workbench application and repository.

SCNSim has no previously accepted or delivered Unit or Runtime API to migrate.
This document records the retained Human-accepted numerical and physical Full
V1 behavior in place while clearly separating the unaccepted structured-
authoring target. It does not supersede, mutate, redirect, or provide
compatibility for the legacy Workbench. Reusable implementation may later be
transplanted only from the exact public handoff with its Git provenance.

## Runtime ownership model {#runtime-ownership-model}

### Four responsibilities

| Object | Owns | Does not own |
|---|---|---|
| `CircuitPlan` | Target physical/structural declaration, components, parameters, buses/taps, canonical ground, logical Ports, and catalog identities | Execution state or results |
| `NetworkViewRef` | One immutable Plan reference and ordered topology/view lineage | Compilation, workspace writes, or results |
| `CircuitRun` | One sealed Plan, workspace, runtime identity, requests, receipts, and execution | Circuit physics or a mutable current model/result |
| typed `AnalysisResult` | One verified request result and its exact evidence identity | Authority to mutate the Plan, Ref, or Run |

### Two users, one reusable model

The public SCNSim vocabulary serves two different layers:

| Layer | Primary objects | Repeated work it should avoid |
|---|---|---|
| Circuit-model development | `Library`, target structured `CircuitPlan`, `NetworkViewRef`, quantity and solve Specs | Re-deriving physical topology, ownership, or analysis semantics in every Notebook |
| Model consumption | A project-owned Design Target and thin Python façade returning typed Results | Restating components, structure, Ports, objective selectors, weights, and optimizer controls |

The façade is ordinary consumer-package code, not a second SCNSim registry or
physical authority. It reconstructs the exact Plan/Ref/Spec request, so a
kernel-restarted consumer can call the same façade to `resolve()` exact durable
evidence. The model developer may expose `optimize_readout(target, workspace)`
or another domain-named function; SCNSim does not prescribe those project
names and does not own their Design Target.

The current native-API engineer course keeps those responsibilities visible
instead of wrapping them in a project façade. It begins with
[one complete physical circuit](../examples/engineer/chapter-01/01-build.qmd),
then teaches [points and Optimization](../examples/engineer/chapter-02/01-build.qmd),
[a custom Library and Composite](../examples/engineer/chapter-05/01-library.qmd),
[complete RLGC values](../examples/engineer/chapter-07/01-rlgc.qmd), and
[restart-safe report/resolve](../examples/engineer/chapter-08/01-persist.qmd).
PTC, transformed Views, scalar response lookup, and independent Direct/HB
Results remain in [Chapter 4](../examples/engineer/chapter-04/01-physical-plan.qmd).

This separation is a UX boundary, not a second Runtime. Both users ultimately
receive the same typed SCNSim Results and exact receipt identities.

`CircuitPlan` is the only physical circuit authority. There is no
`ReducedCircuitPlan`; a Schur-complement model is an analysis reference derived
from the Plan, not a second circuit.

Calculation and Parameter resolution consume the shared frozen assembly model
without importing diagram modules or requiring a successful layout. Diagram
state cannot mutate the Plan, parameter definitions, or numerical requests.
An externally open Composite interface is legal assembly, not a promise of
numerical solvability; required native terminals and physical checks remain.

### Component authoring supplies the Plan

The [Component Authoring Contract](component-authoring.qmd) retains immutable
built-in/custom Libraries and physical factory/lowering semantics. The
[structured-authoring target](contracts/circuit-plan-assembly.qmd#structured-authoring-grammar)
owns the proposed public assembly grammar. Its shortest target route is:

```python
from scnsim import CircuitPlan, components, units as u

plan = CircuitPlan(id="example")
readout_cap = plan.add(
    components.capacitor(
        id="readout_cap",
        capacitance=92.0 * u.fF,
    )
)
readout_bus = plan.bus(id="readout")
plan.branch(
    id="readout_capacitance",
    at=readout_bus,
    elements=(readout_cap,),
    end=plan.ground,
)
```

Every Plan owns one canonical ground. The target exposes it as `scope.ground`,
a local endpoint for intrinsic structured branches. Parent-applied external
grounding instead uses `ground_pins(pins=(...))` on eligible public pins;
ordinary zero-wire connections use `link(endpoints=(...))` and cannot accept a
`GroundRef`. Direct uses the one resulting reference as node flux ground and HB
lowers it to JosephsonCircuits node `"0"`; the backend spelling is not a public
coordinate.
Ordinary two-terminal native bodies retain factory-defined terminal order and
require exactly one structural use. Complete Composite occurrences and native
multi-terminal bodies may instead remain independent peers after complete pin
binding, or may be used once in a compatible structure. `.between()` supplies
an ordered pair only for that structural use.

Every public physical value uses the one `scnsim.units` Pint registry. Public
physical inputs do not accept bare numbers; a physically meaningful
dimensionless value uses `u.dimensionless`. Counts, indices, seeds, booleans,
enum choices, and other non-physical controls remain ordinary Python values.

The Runtime consumes the authored Plan. It does not maintain a mutable Library,
invent child-component parameters, or infer topology or units from a component
name.

### Seal one Plan into one Run

`CircuitRun` seals the Plan and binds it to one evidence workspace:

```python
from scnsim import CircuitRun

run = CircuitRun(
    plan=plan,
    workspace="results/example_run",
    versioned=False,
)

original = run.original
```

The Run has no global `action`, current Ref, current parameters, or current
result. `versioned=False` is the default topology-iteration policy: opening the
same workspace with a different successfully sealed Plan atomically replaces
the prior Plan workspace and its request evidence without a confirmation
prompt. Opening it with the same Plan identity reuses the existing workspace.

`versioned=True` preserves topologies beneath the selected parent workspace as
`iteration01`, `iteration02`, and so on. Each iteration is a complete ordinary
Plan workspace; the parent index maps Plan identity to iteration, and the same
Plan reuses its existing directory. Changing a Spec or ParameterSet alone does
not allocate an iteration.

An existing unversioned workspace may be upgraded atomically to
`versioned=True`; its current Plan becomes `iteration01` without changing its
requests. The reverse transition is forbidden before mutation because it would
delete evidence the user explicitly chose to preserve. The error directs the
user to supply a different workspace path for replacement mode.

Construction first captures and completely validates one authoring snapshot,
resolves its baseline, derives its canonical identity and original View, and
prepares the prospective workspace binding. It does not recapture the Plan or
rerun `complete()` after commit. Under the existing exclusive workspace lock,
an unchanged pointer is verified in place; a changed active pointer is
atomically published with any exact old-leaf cleanup intent. That logical
commit is confirmed through the platform's native publication barriers, then
the supplied Plan is sealed from the already-validated state and the Run is
returned. Linux/macOS retain file flush, atomic replace and directory `fsync`.
The Windows JAX candidate flushes written regular files with `FlushFileBuffers`,
uses same-volume `MoveFileExW(REPLACE_EXISTING | WRITE_THROUGH)` without a
copy/delete fallback, and issues `FlushFileBuffers` on an actual directory
handle opened with `FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS` and write access. Access or
unsupported-handle failures remain native failures; no directory barrier is
silently skipped. These are OS-native guarantees, not an assertion about
arbitrary hardware power loss.

Ordinary failure before pointer publication returns no Run, leaves an initially
editable Plan editable, and preserves the previously active workspace leaf.
Only exact hidden staging owned by the workspace grammar may be removed or
recovered. If the pointer may have published but durability or state
confirmation fails, SCNSim cannot safely infer rollback: it seals the prepared
Plan, returns no Run, and raises `WorkspaceCommitIndeterminateError` at
`workspace_commit` with Plan/workspace identity evidence and an explicit
`plan_sealed=True`, `workspace_may_have_changed=True` state.
On Windows an issued write-through move combines rename and flush in one native
result. If that call returns a native failure, logical-pointer publication is
conservatively indeterminate with the actual error as its cause. Pre-move
path/write/file-flush errors are not classified this way, and potentially
published state is retained for its existing recovery owner.

Windows JAX Workspace support uses the same root, request, operation and store
ownership order, backed by native shared/exclusive byte-range locks on the
stable lock files. Nonblocking idle contention is distinct from other native
failures. Regular file paths are `Path` values; readonly SQLite URIs are derived
with `Path.as_uri()`, while artifact identities retain their normalized logical
POSIX-relative names. Memory mode does not acquire these storage locks or
create a Workspace.  Native filesystem publication and its uncertain tail retain their
own contract; successful locking does not replace a durability barrier.

Old-leaf deletion is postcommit maintenance and cannot turn a successfully
committed Run into constructor failure. The active root retains one bounded,
typed cleanup-pending record until the exact retired leaf is absent and that
state is durably republished. Workspace maintenance retains these
records independently of request rows. A later normal exclusive operation may
finish only the classified leaf, but first validates the active pointer and its
complete active evidence. Active corruption, absence, or stale binding
ownership preserves the retired leaf and maintenance record for diagnosis;
SCNSim neither adopts nor deletes unknown orphans and runs no background
cleaner.

Sealing is permanent for both that Run and the supplied Python Plan. The same
`CircuitRun` may execute any number of immutable Refs, Specs, and ParameterSets
derived from its sealed Plan; none
of those questions changes the Plan or invalidates earlier Results. Editing
sealed Plan content—including topology, an authoring baseline, Ports,
couplings, or a public component schema—raises `PlanSealedError`. The author
reruns the builder to create a new `CircuitPlan` and `CircuitRun`; the same
Python variable names and workspace path may be rebound without restarting the
kernel. Supplying a declared `ParameterSet` does not change topology.

In replacement mode, an older Run or lazy Result fails with
`WorkspacePlanReplacedError` once another Plan has replaced its backing
workspace. The check binds an evidence-only workspace-instance ID in addition
to the Plan hash, so an `A → B → A` sequence cannot accidentally revive the old
A handle. With `versioned=True`, each Run remains bound to its retained
iteration and may coexist with newer topology Runs.

### Declare the floating-qubit Ref graph without executing {#floating-qubit-ref-graph}

`run.original` is the zero-reduction root `NetworkViewRef`. `reduce()` returns
a new immutable Ref and never compiles, solves, or writes saved
evidence:

```python
compensated = original.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().ptc(
        probe_plus,
        probe_minus,
    )
)

qubit_modes = compensated.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().transform_pair(
        "qubit_plus",
        "qubit_minus",
        id="qubit",
    )
)

qubit_differential = qubit_modes.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().retain(
        "qubit.differential",
    )
)

feedline = qubit_modes.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().retain(
        "feedline_in",
        "feedline_out",
    )
)

monitoring = qubit_modes.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().retain(
        "feedline_in",
        "feedline_out",
        "monitor",
    )
)
```

Here `probe_plus` and `probe_minus` are the `PortRef` handles returned when the
Plan added the two logical probe Ports. `ptc()` removes their selected,
evidenced load stamps from the effective analysis topology.
`transform_pair()` replaces the ordered Public node pair with the generated
`qubit.common` and `qubit.differential` coordinates. `retain()` selects an
ordered, non-empty set of Public or generated node coordinates and
Schur-eliminates the complete complement under `I_external = 0`. None of these
declarations executes work.

The reusable point is the Ref itself:
`original -> compensated -> qubit_modes -> feedline`. A Ref may produce any
number of child Refs, so the same transformed ancestor can support a one-port
differential view, a two-port feedline view, and a larger monitoring view.
Pipeline step labels are evidence labels, not a second API such as
`model.at("checkpoint")`.

## Run operations and durable results

### One execution owner {#solve-versus-evaluate}

The Run performs every terminal operation, but `solve()` and `evaluate()` have
different user-visible jobs:

| Question | Call | Compatible Spec family | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| What is the selected-view S/Y/Z response over a grid? | `run.solve(ref, spec)` | `DirectSolveSpec` | Direct response matrices and named traces |
| What is one Direct root, pole, zero, coupling, or response scalar? | `run.evaluate(ref, spec)` | Typed Direct quantity Spec | Typed quantity Result |
| What is the complete Direct dynamic operator? | `run.evaluate(ref, spec)` | `OperatorSpec` | `OperatorResult` |
| Which parameters minimize declared typed quantity objectives? | `run.optimize(spec)` or `run.optimize(default_view, spec)` | `OptimizationSpec` | `OptimizationResult` |

The `SolveSpec` suffix means “produce a response surface.” A
`DirectSolveSpec` solves the complete selected-view N-port response over its
declared grid. It does not guess S21: a one-port view yields S11, a two-port
view yields the complete 2-by-2 response, and an N-port view yields the
complete N-by-N response. Named `SParameterTrace` objects are typed projections
of that same result and never launch another solve.
`SolveSpec` is only the category name used by this contract; V1 does not add an
abstract public `SolveSpec` class. Consumers construct `DirectSolveSpec` or
the corresponding typed Spec directly.

The stabilized Full V1 runtime supports `DirectSolveSpec` on every final View that proves
its ordered terminal basis is Port-realizable. It publishes the complete
finite N-port S/Y/Z matrices once, then projects any declared named traces from
that same result. A non-realizable final View fails closed rather than
returning an incomplete or fabricated wave response.

A Direct quantity Spec instead asks `evaluate()` for one defined physical
quantity without creating an unrelated response sweep. `DiagonalRootSpec`
selects one named diagonal of the complete final View operator and returns its
machine-resolved root, frequency, linewidth, and local slope. The coordinate
must belong to that View's ordered terminal basis; the basis need not be a
singleton. `OperatorElementRootSpec(row, column, root_hint)` selects a named
ordered element of that same operator and returns its locally simple complex
root, real-part frequency, and slope $dF_{row,column}/d\omega$. Unlike a
diagonal root, it imposes no passive-imaginary-root policy and has no linewidth
selector. Neither Spec reduces the final View a second time. Their coordinate
handles own physical identity; `root_hint` only initializes the baseline Newton
basin.
`ResponseElementSpec` may
evaluate one explicitly selected S/Y/Z scalar at one frequency, but it still
does not imply a frequency-grid response. `OperatorSpec` is the deliberate
exception that materializes the complete labeled Direct operator.

These combinations fail closed before execution:

```python
run.solve(feedline, DiagonalRootSpec(...))
run.evaluate(feedline, DirectSolveSpec(...))
```

The valid operations remain independent exact requests:

```python
direct = run.solve(feedline, DirectSolveSpec(...))
```

`solve()`, `evaluate()`, and `optimize()` are real actions. They compute the
exact request identity, materialize missing dependencies in order, write
sealed request/receipt/artifact evidence, and return the corresponding typed
Result. They do not mutate the Plan or Ref and do not save a result as mutable
state on the Run.

Presentation is never another action:

```python
from scnsim import Theme

direct.s.show(magnitude="db", theme=Theme.AUTO)
direct.traces["transmission"].show(magnitude="db", theme=Theme.DARK)
readout.show()
```

These calls read the typed Results already returned above. They do not solve,
recompute, interpolate, or select a latest request.

### Use response and quantity Results together

One Notebook may legitimately need both the response surface and a physical
quantity. It declares two Specs and executes two explicit requests against the
same sealed Run and Ref:

```python
reflection_trace = SParameterTrace(
    id="reflection",
    input_port="signal_in",
    input_mode=(),
    output_port="signal_in",
    output_mode=(),
)
direct_spec = DirectSolveSpec(
    frequencies=frequency_grid,
    traces=(reflection_trace,),
)
root_spec = DiagonalRootSpec(
    coordinate="readout_node",
    root_hint=6.0 * u.GHz,
)

direct = run.solve(view, direct_spec)
root = run.evaluate(view, root_spec)

report = run.build_report(
    ReportSpec(inputs=(direct, root), theme=Theme.AUTO)
)
```

The two requests may reuse exact sealed compile/dependency evidence, but there
is no hidden current Result and neither request changes the meaning of the
other. The Report records both exact input identities rather than deriving the
root from a plotted S minimum or pretending the diagonal root is S21.

### Request identity and immutable attempts {#request-identity-and-immutable-attempts}

A canonical request identifies the sealed Plan, Ref, Spec, ParameterSet,
runtime, and operation. Execution history is not part of that identity. If the
request already has one complete verified success receipt, the operation
reuses that Result without recomputing or overwriting it.

The Run validates and normalizes those declarations once into a private
immutable prepared analysis before canonical encoding. Prepared data is
declarative: it carries no executable Run, workspace, process callback,
candidate realization, or mutable live-read path. For optimization, each bound
leaf retains objective ID plus authored objective/term order, while dependency
sharing remains keyed by the complete View and root/quantity Spec rather than
by the leaf's objective identity. The canonical request encoder formats only
this prepared data; it does not choose a View, resolve parameters, or read a
later baseline value again.

Execution coordination may consume the canonical request and workspace owner,
but it does not decode an unchecked producer payload. Workspace verification
first establishes the sealed request/attempt/receipt/result chain. Typed Result
decoding consumes that verified-success record independently and cannot turn a
producer assertion into authorization. Immediate path-backed decoding remains
inside that ownership-checked reader or writer interval. Deferred sweep reads
reacquire the original binding's reader and revalidate the exact request,
attempt, receipt, and Result seals before validating and reading only the
requested chunk or point payload. They do not rescan every sweep payload; a
replacement leaf raises `WorkspacePlanReplacedError`. Detached materialized
values may outlive the interval. These private ownership boundaries do not add
a public Job, prepared-request, or decoder API.

The workspace path is an evidence location, not part of computational request
identity. A leaf workspace binds one Plan; each request binds its semantic
runtime. `CircuitRun` resolves the request only inside that Plan workspace. A
different or relocated workspace does not rename the request, but it may not
contain the required receipt.

If every prior attempt failed or was interrupted, calling the same operation
again keeps the canonical request identity and appends a new immutable attempt.
Earlier requests, logs, failure receipts, and partial artifacts remain
auditable; there is no force-overwrite flag and no mutable current attempt.
Only the operation methods create attempts. `resolve()` never retries, resumes,
or launches work.

Attempt ordinals start at one and use a minimum width of six decimal digits:
`attempts/000001/`, `attempts/000002/`, and so on. Values beyond six digits
grow naturally without an artificial maximum. Before promotion, the same
ordinal appears in
the leaf-relative
`.scnsim-workspace-staging/<operation-UUIDv4>/<request-sha256>/.staging-000001-<lowercase-canonical-UUIDv4>/`.
This is the actual centralized staging path, not a logical identifier. An ordinal spelling,
UUID form, final directory, or staging directory that does not match its
sealed attempt evidence fails integrity validation; path formatting is not an
implementation choice.

### Explain before execution

V1 does not expose a public JobRef layer. A consumer can inspect a request
without executing it:

```python
run.explain(feedline, direct_spec).show()
```

`explain()` performs the same deterministic ParameterSet binding and compile
preflight needed to resolve topology and coordinate evidence, but it does not
launch a solver, create a request directory, or write the workspace. The
explanation identifies the sealed Plan, selected Ref, effective parameters,
operation/backend, grids, reduction lineage, runtime, and exact dependency
graph. It expands every component to its backend rows, shows Library/schema
identity, component-pin to electric-node/ground mapping, Public/Internal/
Port-promoted node identities, zero-wire link membership, intrinsic and
parent-applied grounding provenance, logical Port attachments and namespace
mapping,
Direct `B`/`Y0`/load/wave lowering, HB `P`/`R_port` lowering,
SQUID loop orientation, and every bound inductive-coupling `L1`, `L2`, signed
`k`, derived `M`, and backend map. For an automatic paired-node transform it
also shows every included
external-cut capacitance branch, every excluded direct-mutual branch, the
resolved weights and transform, the transformed reference matrix and principal
root, Port-realizability, and the ordered mode-port realization. It also lists
the retained/eliminated coordinates, final selected-view channel order,
induced `A_k`/`B_k`/`R_k`/`D_k`, and per-probe raw/compensated load state. HB
explanations additionally show the exact source-coefficient index/conjugation
map, signed nonzero response frequencies, and input/output `W` conversion for
solver-native Z and S.
Optimization explanations show
each required root hint and baseline branch selection, the expanded relative or
explicit residual scales, quantity dependency graph, shared
compile/factorization/root work and baseline
resolution; candidate-specific continuations remain in candidate receipts.

### Resolve without execution

`resolve()` accepts the same Ref, Spec, and parameter selection as its
corresponding operation. The [Parameter System Contract](contracts/parameter-system.qmd#parameterized-operations)
owns point/space resolution and optimization's fixed non-active input binding;
active variables still start at their sealed baseline. `explain()` retains its
separately declared preflight surface:

```python
direct = run.resolve(feedline, direct_spec)
```

It recomputes the expected request identity, then reads and verifies the sealed
workspace request, receipt, and artifacts. It never executes, searches for a
latest stage, retries a failed or interrupted attempt, or relies on a
process-local cache. The same call must therefore work after a Notebook kernel
restart when every bound identity remains exact. Missing, stale, corrupt, or
mismatched evidence fails closed with the missing or mismatched identity named.

## Units, identity, and parameter variants

### Canonical SI identity

At every Python trust boundary, SCNSim validates Quantity dimensionality and
normalizes physical values to coherent SI for compilation and hashing:

```text
SCNSim-registry Quantity
-> validate declared dimensionality
-> canonical SI magnitude + SI unit
-> compile/request identity
```

The sealed representation records:

- canonical SI magnitude and unit;
- physical dimensionality;
- preferred declaration/display unit; and
- original input magnitude and unit as provenance.

Receipts do not pickle Pint objects. They serialize magnitudes, units, and
dimensionality so another process can reconstruct a Quantity with the same
SCNSim registry. This follows Pint's guidance for a shared application
registry and durable serialization:

- [Using Pint in a project](https://pint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/getting/pint-in-your-projects.html)
- [Serializing Pint quantities](https://pint.readthedocs.io/en/stable/advanced/serialization.html)

Physically identical `92.0 * u.fF` and `0.092 * u.pF` produce the same
computational identity after canonicalization. Their source units remain
visible provenance and may be displayed differently without splitting the
physical request identity.
The receipt preserves the source spelling used by the executed attempt. A
later semantic-equivalent reuse returns that verified evidence and does not
append a new attempt merely to log the caller's alternate spelling.

### Static and runtime checks

Public type annotations require `pint.Quantity` with the appropriate magnitude
container, which lets static analysis reject an ordinary float passed to a
Quantity-only interface. Pint's generic annotation does not encode physical
dimensionality, so F-versus-H correctness is enforced at runtime by
`ParameterSpec`, Plan seal, `ParameterSet`, and operation-boundary validation.
SCNSim does not add a parallel phantom-type unit system. See
[Pint typing](https://pint.readthedocs.io/en/stable/advanced/typing.html).

### Explicit ParameterSet variants {#explicit-parameterset-variants}

::: {.callout-warning}
The `CONVERGING` [Parameter System Contract](contracts/parameter-system.qmd)
owns independent definition identity, physical-consumer closure, points,
`ParameterSpace`, sweep Results, and parameterized diagrams. Its implementation
baseline is integrated; no compatibility with legacy envelopes is promised.
:::

The sealed Plan supplies the baseline parameters. An operation may instead
receive an immutable `ParameterSet` keyed by independently defined refs that
the Plan consumes. Rebuild the earlier fixed-value example with a real binding
before sealing; lookup cannot turn its literal into a parameter:

```python
from scnsim import DirectSolveSpec, ParameterDefinitions, ParameterSet, ParameterSpec

inputs = ParameterDefinitions(id="readout_inputs")
capacitance = inputs.parameter(
    id="capacitance", baseline=92.0 * u.fF, spec=ParameterSpec(unit=u.fF)
)
plan = CircuitPlan(id="parameterized_readout")
readout_cap = plan.add(
    components.capacitor(id="readout_cap", capacitance=capacitance)
)
readout_bus = plan.bus(id="readout")
plan.branch(
    id="readout_capacitance", at=readout_bus,
    elements=(readout_cap,), end=plan.ground,
)
plan.add_port(
    id="signal_in", at=readout_bus, role="terminated",
    reference_impedance=50.0 * u.ohm,
)
run = CircuitRun(plan=plan, workspace="results/parameterized_readout")
candidate = ParameterSet({
    readout_cap.parameter("capacitance"): 95.0 * u.fF,
})

candidate_direct = run.solve(
    run.original,
    DirectSolveSpec(frequencies=frequency_grid),
    parameters=candidate,
)
```

Omitting `parameters=` uses the sealed baseline. Supplying a ParameterSet does
not bind or mutate the Ref; the ParameterSet is part of that operation's exact
request identity. A ParameterSet with unknown refs, incompatible units,
non-finite values, or unconsumed/incompatible definitions fails before execution.

Optimization exposes its selected parameters through the same type:

```python
optimization = run.optimize(feedline, optimization_spec)

winner_hb = run.solve(
    feedline,
    final_hb_spec,
    parameters=optimization.best.parameters,
)
```

## Shared topology and unified node views {#shared-topology-and-unified-node-views}

`ReductionPipeline` is one ordered, backend-neutral node-coordinate lineage.
It does not choose an operation. A topology step changes the effective circuit
analyzed by descendants; a view step changes the coordinates or boundary used
to inspect that circuit. Both backends consume the same Ref and either realize
it faithfully or fail before solver execution.

### Selective Port-Termination Compensation (PTC) is a shared topology step

The `ptc()` step explicitly receives one or more `nonloading_probe` `PortRef`
handles from the same Plan:

```python
compensated = run.original.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().ptc(
        probe_plus,
        probe_minus,
    )
)
```

For every selected Port, the sealed compiled artifact must prove one exact
node attachment, finite positive reference impedance, load stamp, and
backend-lowering identity. The explicit `ptc()` call supplies removal intent;
the Port role or a caller-provided resistance alone does not. Physical and
environmental loads that are not selected remain in the effective circuit.

A lineage may contain PTC at most once. It must precede `transform_pair()` and
`retain()`, and every descendant Ref inherits the same compensation set.
`retain()` is the terminal basis selection for that lineage. Unknown, repeated,
terminated, foreign, or unevidenced targets fail before execution.

For Direct analysis, the source-loaded operator first supports the raw solve;
the selected-network adapter then de-embeds all source resistors and re-adds
only the omitted, non-PTC matched loads according to the common load mask.
This is algebraically the explicit removal of each selected probe stamp, but it
does not confuse a selected source resistor with DUT admittance. SCNSim owns:

```text
C: capacitance
K: stiffness / inverse inductance
G: conductance
D(omega) = K - omega^2 C - i omega G
```

Current JAX Direct optimization refreshes each candidate's physical coefficients
and View-dependent operands through the shared fixed-stage program, including
the declared PTC and View lineage. It does not recompile that program merely
because runtime parameter values change. The shared program evaluates
the declared loading boundary rather than a nominal matrix retaining an
artificial loss channel removed by that declaration.

### Automatic paired-node coordinates are a shared view step

`transform_pair()` declares one ordered pair of distinct Public node
coordinates and one output namespace. Inputs may be Plan `ElectricNodeRef`
handles, composite `CoordinateRef` handles, or declared coordinate-ID strings:

```python
qubit_modes = compensated.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().transform_pair(
        "qubit_plus",
        "qubit_minus",
        id="qubit",
    )
)
```

The two inputs are replaced by the ordered outputs `qubit.common` and
`qubit.differential`. The Ref stores the input pair, output namespace, and the
automatic rule; it never stores nominal numeric weights and V1 exposes no
manual-weight override through this operation.

The scientific definition is canonical in
[Admittance Coordinate Transforms](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/network-modeling/admittance-coordinate-transforms.qmd#full-external-cut-weighting).
After binding the operation's complete ParameterSet, SCNSim enumerates the
original compiled reciprocal lumped capacitance branches. Each node's
external cut includes capacitance to ground/reference and to every node outside
the selected pair; every direct mutual branch between the selected nodes is
excluded from the weights but remains in the differential energy and compiled
operator.

This rule selects deterministic floating-pair coordinates. It does not claim
to diagonalize a loaded network, a frequency-dependent admittance, an already
Schur-reduced environment, a distributed model, or an operating-point
linearization. External coordinates may remain coupled to both generated
coordinates.

PTC and `transform_pair()` are independent declarations. A transform neither
requires nor inserts PTC and may act on ordinary Public nodes or nodes with
logical Port attachments. If a lineage contains both, the explicit PTC step
comes first so the topology change remains visible; PTC changes evidenced
conductance stamps and does not change capacitance-derived weights.

Direct operations apply the resolved power-conjugate transform to the selected
operator. HB repeats that same real transform independently inside every
retained sideband mode. Direct optimization resolves the external cut again
from every candidate's original compiled capacitance operator rather than
reusing baseline weights.

The selected-view S matrix uses the generalized real-SPD matrix-reference
power-wave contract from
[Port Reference Impedance Semantics](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/simulation/port-reference-impedance-semantics.qmd#real-spd-matrix-reference-power-waves).
SCNSim transforms the declared physical reference matrix with the resolved
coordinate map and uses its principal symmetric SPD square root. It does not
replace a non-diagonal transformed reference with diagonal entries. Direct and
HB therefore expose the same selected-view wave convention even when the
backend-native HB convention differs.

### Retain an arbitrary node-coordinate view

`retain()` accepts any ordered, non-empty set of unique Public or generated
coordinates from the current basis. A selector is a Plan `ElectricNodeRef`, a
composite-exposed `CoordinateRef`, or a declared coordinate-ID string. Handles
