are preferred while authoring one live Plan. Strings are required for
transform-generated coordinates and remain valid for named or Port-promoted
Public coordinates at serialized/team-facade boundaries:

```python
feedline = compensated.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().retain(
        feedline_in_node,
        feedline_out_node,
    )
)

filter_quantities = compensated.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().retain(
        ipf.coordinate("filter_open_tail"),
    )
)
```

The listed coordinates become the selected-view order. Every coordinate in the
complete complement is dynamically Schur-eliminated with zero external current
while loads already present in the effective operator remain. Anonymous
Internal nodes are never directly selectable and therefore remain in that
complement. `N=1` and `N=2` are ordinary one- and two-coordinate cases, not
separate APIs.

The selected-view wave-channel ID is exactly its final retained coordinate ID.
For an original node this is its Public node ID; for an automatic transform it
is the generated ID such as `qubit.differential`. A logical Port ID is not a
channel alias. Only anonymous-node promotion deliberately makes a node ID equal
to its Port ID. Unknown or foreign handles/IDs, generated-output collisions,
and duplicate retained identities fail before any trace is bound. A
`CoordinateRef` can be observed but is not a structured-authoring endpoint and
cannot be passed to `add_port()`; the owning scope must expose a separate
`PinRef` for parent wiring. Root Ports attach only to a root `BusRef` or
`TapRef`.

A probe-free feedline S21 therefore requires both operations:

1. `ptc()` removes the artificial probe shunt; and
2. `retain()` excludes that probe coordinate from the selected external set.

If a compensated probe remains in the retained set, a requested S matrix still
applies its declared matched-wave boundary. Energy coupled into that retained
external port is correct N-port scattering behavior, not a failed PTC.

Zero-current coordinate elimination is the boundary operation described by
[Schur Complement and Kron Reduction](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/numerical-methods/schur-complement-kron-reduction.qmd#zero-current-schur-versus-matched-wave-submatrices).
It is not equivalent to selecting the same rows and columns from a native S
matrix, because omitted native incident waves leave those ports terminated in
their wave references.

#### Static capacitance on a retained View

This static-capacitance rule is the CONVERGING dev36 extension; established
View and dynamic-operation behavior remains unchanged.

For static capacitance, the View owns the ordered retained coordinates and the
Spec selects the physical C equation: `StaticCapacitanceSpec()` has no
`zero_charge` input. Without `retain()`, evaluation returns the full finite C
in the selected transformed basis. With `retain()`, the selected coordinates
are the retained order and the complete finite complement—including internal
finite-pi coordinates—is eliminated by

$$
C_{\mathrm{eff}}=C_{rr}-C_{re}\,\operatorname{solve}(C_{ee},C_{er}),
\qquad q_e=0.
$$

The partition and zero-charge condition are derived from the View and retained
as result/evidence facts. A valid PTC lineage may precede transform and retain;
its resistive/reference load mask does not change static C or transform
weights. Static C does not require response-port eligibility or apply RF
normalization. Existing Direct dynamic response, operator, root, and
residue-coupling paths keep their dynamic Schur equations and existing
zero-external-current boundary. See the
[static-capacitance contract](contracts/static-capacitance.qmd)
and [guide](guides/static-capacitance.qmd).

### Terminal-operation capability

The pipeline vocabulary stays common while terminal operations enforce what
they can physically publish:

| Selected coordinate | Direct `evaluate()` / `optimize()` | Direct `solve()` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Public node without a logical Port | Yes | No |
| Public node with one logical Port | Yes | Yes |
| Generated coordinate from an invertible transform of a complete Port-bound node subspace | Yes | Yes |
| Generated coordinate involving a non-Port-bound node | Yes | No |
| Anonymous Internal node | Not directly selectable | Not directly selectable |

`solve()` always promises a complete selected-view S/Y/Z surface, so every
final coordinate must be port-realizable: either one original node with a
unique logical Port, or a generated coordinate from an invertible transform of
a complete Port-bound node subspace. Direct does not return a special
matrix-only solve result when this is false; it fails closed. Direct
`evaluate()` and `optimize()` may still inspect a named unported Public node in
the complete node operator because they do not promise a wave-port response.

When no explicit `retain()` exists, `solve()` uses all logical Ports in Plan
declaration order. `evaluate()` and Direct `optimize()` may instead work from
the full node operator and their named quantity selectors. HB may omit some
Port-bound nodes from the selected view: its full nonlinear/static balance
still includes every logical Port and load, then the linearized raw Z/Y
operator eliminates omitted channels with `I_external = 0`.

### One logical Port, two backend lowerings

A logical Port is a specialized `CircuitPlan` component, not a Library factory
and not a JosephsonCircuits row exposed as the product API:

| Port content | Direct | HB / JosephsonCircuits |
|---|---|---|
| Node attachment | incidence/selector column `B` | resolved node of `P_i` and `R_port_i` |
| Reference impedance | `Y0 = 1 / R0` and power-wave conversion | explicit `R_port_i` and solver port impedance |
| Port marker | no `P` row | exact `P_i` row |
| Source/load boundary | `G_port = B Y0 B^T` during raw solve | explicit source resistor stamp |
| Drive | external current injection through `B` | mode-indexed current on `P_i` |
| PTC | clear proved probe entry in the post-de-embedding load mask | clear the same proved probe entry in every sideband load mask |

The load and wave reference are separately auditable. PTC removes only the
load stamp; it preserves the logical Port identity, node coordinate, and
reference impedance required to define the selected S surface. Direct never
creates a fake `P` element merely to resemble the HB backend. Its receipt says
`P row = not applicable` and records the actual selector, reference-admittance,
voltage/current, load, and wave-conversion mapping. HB records the exact `P_i`
and `R_port_i` rows, solver indices, modes, and port order.

For both lowerings, Port voltage is the attached-node voltage relative to the
Plan ground and positive Port current enters the Plan at that node. The
canonical node attachment therefore owns direction; there is no backend- or
request-specific orientation override.

The logical Port resistance is a wave/source boundary, not a DUT shunt in the
public network. It participates in the raw solve and therefore supplies the
external damping of the solved problem, but SCNSim de-embeds the selected
source boundary before publishing `.y.view`, `.z.view`, and `.s.view`.

Let `B_p` inject the ordered original logical-Port currents into the full node
basis and let

$$
R_p=\operatorname{diag}(R_1,\ldots,R_P),
\qquad D_p=R_p^{1/2}.
$$

After backend normalization, SCNSim first removes *all* backend `P + R` source
resistors to recover the intrinsic linearized circuit operator. PTC then
defines a diagonal original-Port load mask `M`: `M[i,i] = 0` only for an
explicitly selected `nonloading_probe`; every other logical Port load remains
active. This mask is independent of whether a Port is retained or omitted.

For a Port-realizable selected view, let $A_k$ map ordered original-Port
voltages to the final retained voltages. Power-conjugate injection and the
matrix reference are

$$
B_k=B_pA_k^T,
\qquad R_k=A_kR_pA_k^T,
\qquad D_k=R_k^{1/2}.
$$

`D_k` is the principal real-SPD square root. Define the power-wave row map and
its selected/omitted projectors in original Port space:

$$
Q_k=D_k^{-1}A_kD_p,
\qquad P_k=Q_k^TQ_k,
\qquad P_o=I-P_k.
$$

These wave-boundary objects exist only when the terminal View is
Port-realizable. Retaining an unported Public node does not turn that node into
a Port and does not define $A_k$, $B_k$, $R_k$, $D_k$, $Q_k$, $P_k$, $P_o$, or
an omitted matched-load matrix. Its lineage stores the canonical not-applicable
representation for every such field: an `evidenceMatrix` with `rows=0` and
`columns=0`, whose SHA-256 covers the closed
`applicability=not_port_realizable` envelope. The source-boundary and
de-embedding hashes cover matching closed not-applicable envelopes. This is an
identity sentinel, not a zero-valued physical Port model.

The retained node and its complement remain exact node-coordinate lineage.
Direct quantity evaluation forms the complete loaded node operator—including
every logical-Port load not removed by PTC—and Schur-eliminates the complement
under zero external current. It may therefore evaluate a loaded node root.
`solve()` fails capability preflight on the same View before execution because
no S/Y/Z wave network exists there.

V1 requires a transformed pair to have one common load state: both original
Port loads are selected by PTC or neither is. That restriction makes the
retained and load partitions separable. A mixed-state pair fails preflight
rather than silently assigning a fractional load to the generated channels.
The omitted matched-load conductance in original Port coordinates is

$$
G_{o,p}=D_p^{-1}P_oMP_oD_p^{-1}.
$$

Let $Y_{\mathrm{circ,node}}$ be the intrinsic, source-resistor-de-embedded
Direct node admittance. SCNSim applies this exact
selected-network order:

1. add omitted matched loads,
   $H=Y_{\mathrm{circ,node}}+B_pG_{o,p}B_p^T$;
2. add only the selected source boundary and solve
   $$
   Z_{\mathrm{src},k}
   =B_k^T(H+B_kR_k^{-1}B_k^T)^{-1}B_k;
   $$
3. obtain $Y_{\mathrm{src},k}$ by a matrix solve and de-embed the selected
   source boundary,
   $$Y_{\mathrm{net},k}=Y_{\mathrm{src},k}-R_k^{-1};$$
4. form public $Z_{\mathrm{net},k}$ from that same network Y; and
5. form the matrix-reference power-wave response

$$
\widetilde Y_k=D_kY_{\mathrm{net},k}D_k,
\qquad
S^{\mathrm{view}}=(I+\widetilde Y_k)^{-1}(I-\widetilde Y_k).
$$

Every inverse symbol above defines an equation, not an implementation method;
factorizations and linear solves are required. A rank-deficient $A_k$,
non-SPD $R_k$, singular selected solve, or incompatible load partition fails
closed.

The three public families now describe one de-embedded network:

$$
Y^{\mathrm{view}}=Y_{\mathrm{net},k},\qquad
Z^{\mathrm{view}}=Z_{\mathrm{net},k},\qquad
S^{\mathrm{view}}=S(Y_{\mathrm{net},k},R_k).
$$

An open one-port therefore has `Y_net = 0` and `S11 = +1`; a DUT whose
intrinsic input admittance is `1 / R0` has `S11 = 0`. Omitted terminated Ports
remain matched environmental loads. PTC changes only the explicitly selected
probe entries of `M`; it never de-embeds an unrelated physical/environmental
load. The typed matrix view continues to record each relevant probe as `raw`
or `compensated`, but the selected source boundary is never mislabeled as DUT.

### HB PTC operator realization

HB V1 is removed from 1.0. See the retained [HB V1 History](implementation/hb-realization-and-outcomes.qmd).

### Named HB drives, cases, mixing, and driven PTC {#named-hb-drives-cases-and-mixing}

HB V1 is removed from 1.0. See the retained [HB V1 History](implementation/hb-realization-and-outcomes.qmd).

### Required lineage and receipt evidence

The durable evidence chain for every terminal `AnalysisResult` binds the sealed
Plan, compiled operator, ParameterSet, ordered Ref lineage,
retained/eliminated coordinates, selected channel order, and exact runtime
identity. Those records remain owned by their canonical Plan, request, Result,
artifact, and receipt documents rather than being duplicated into every public
Result object.

The Plan/compile evidence records every exact Library and component-schema
identity, component hierarchy and public schema, pin-to-electric-node/ground
mapping, Public/Internal/Port-promoted node identities, canonical ground and
backend-node-zero mapping, N-link membership, intrinsic and parent-applied
grounding provenance, logical Port mapping,
source units and canonical SI values, public ParameterRefs, expanded
primitive/backend rows, and Direct realization. Composite evidence includes
public parameters/baselines, identity fan-out, AffineMap equations/support,
public pins/coordinates, and hidden-child expansion. RLGC evidence includes
conductor/reference identity, complete matrix order and health, positive
head-to-tail series-current/extractor `+z` orientation, manual/Q2D source
classification, parsed canonical values, extraction frequency, content-derived
provenance, transmission-line pi-ladder convention, section count, and bound
section length; all three IDC capacitance branches, each JJ
and optional parallel `Cj`, the two shared-parameter
SQUID junctions and finite loop, and every coupled branch orientation with
bound `L1`, `L2`, signed `k`, derived `M`, and backend mapping. The authoring
surface and its fail-closed rules are defined in
[V1 Component Authoring](component-authoring.qmd). The exact recursively sealed
graph and deterministic lowering are fixed in
[Composite Snapshots and Recursive Expansion](implementation/composite-snapshots-and-recursive-expansion.qmd),
while distributed-line parsing and expansion are fixed in
[RLGC, Q2D, and Pi Expansion](implementation/rlgc-q2d-and-pi-expansion.qmd).

In the `dev4` slice, `run.explain()` materializes expanded branch rows,
`omitted-as-zero` labels, and derived mutual-inductance mappings. Terminal
receipts bind the sealed Plan, request, and exact runtime identities; they do
not duplicate those compiler-row diagnostics as a second evidence schema.

A logical Port record includes its identity, role, reference impedance,
node/coordinate attachment, and one-Port-per-node evidence. Direct records
`B`, `Y0`, `G_port`, voltage/current and wave conversion, plus `P row = not
applicable`; HB records exact `P_i`/`R_port_i` rows, solver indices, mode order,
and raw-Z lineage.

A PTC lineage additionally records selected `PortRef` identities, proved load
stamps, original-Port load mask, load state before/after compensation, resolved
resistances, removal intent, raw-Z/derived-intrinsic-operator identities,
per-probe `raw`/`compensated` labels, and reconstruction or residual evidence.

Every `transform_pair()` lineage additionally records its exact ordered Public
node inputs, Port-realizability mapping and current directions, all included
external-cut branches, all
excluded direct-mutual branches, resolved weights, power-conjugate maps,
transformed real-SPD reference matrix, principal root and reconstruction
evidence, and generated coordinate order. These obligations apply whether or
not the lineage contains PTC.

Every `retain()` lineage records the ordered retained coordinates, complete
eliminated complement, final selected-view channel order, and exact
full-row-rank `A_k`, injection `B_k`, induced reference `R_k`, principal root
`D_k`, wave map `Q_k`, selected/omitted projectors, omitted matched loads,
selected source boundary, and public-network de-embedding evidence.
The canonical step order, recomputation boundary, and N-port realization are
fixed in
[View Lineage and Selected Networks](implementation/view-lineage-and-selected-networks.qmd).

Direct quantity and optimization receipts additionally record quantity-spec
identity, selector and dimensionality, root/pole/zero branch and its declared
locator, the `DiagonalRootSpec.root_hint`, baseline selection, continuation and
local slope/residue evidence where applicable, shared dependency nodes, expanded
residual scale and source, objective weight, candidate failure ledger, and the
the actual JAX runtime identity. The canonical optimization request owns
model-default bounds, any immutable consumer overrides, resolved bounds, and
the authorization set. Its receipt retains those roles only transitively by
binding that request hash; receipt-local evidence records AffineMap
support/extrapolation outcomes and authorization provenance, physical candidate
values, dimensionless optimizer coordinates, and the source-unit spelling used
by the executed attempt. It never duplicates a second bounds authority.

### Linear Direct component realization

Direct consumes the expanded Plan. R, L and C rows remain linear, and complete
validated RLGC matrices retain their authored conductor order. Each Josephson
junction uses its declared zero-phase, zero-bias small-signal inductance and
any explicit parallel capacitance. A symmetric SQUID remains an authored
two-junction finite-loop topology with those linear branches.

RLGC acceptance is strict on the canonical Float64 matrices. Reciprocity uses
exact symmetry; Maxwell C/G signs and row sums must already have their required
signs; C/L must pass unpivoted symmetric Cholesky; and the minimum eigenvalue of
G/R must be nonnegative. SCNSim does not symmetrize, clip, project, add a
grounding correction, or retain a corrected matrix beside the raw source.
Failure names the exact matrix invariant rather than manufacturing a usable
line model.

### Operation support

| Selected Ref lineage | Direct evaluate/optimize | Direct solve |
|---|---:|---:|
| Original | Yes | all logical Ports |
| PTC | Yes | Yes |
| `transform_pair()` over a complete Port-bound node pair | Yes | Yes |
| `retain()` of only Port-realizable coordinates | Yes | Yes |
| Named unported Public node or transform involving one | Yes | No |

Physical compilation belongs to the original Plan and is not presented as a
separate reduced compile action. Terminal operations materialize or exactly
resolve the required original and selected-view stages internally.

## Direct matrices and physical quantities

### Common matrix surface

Direct exposes the selected-view S/Y/Z families without pretending
their enclosing Results are identical:

```python
direct.s.view
direct.y.view
direct.z.view
```

For the canonical $e^{-i\omega t}$ convention, the Direct circuit admittance is

$$
Y_{\mathrm{circ}}(\omega)
=\frac{D(\omega)}{-i\omega}
=G-i\omega C+\frac{i}{\omega}K.
$$

`DirectSolveSpec.frequencies` is one SCNSim-registry frequency Quantity whose
magnitude is a non-empty, one-dimensional, finite grid with every $f>0$.
Direct and Operator response requests retain the exact declared occurrence
order, including repeated frequencies and reverse grids. Shared fixed-frequency
work may reuse an identical declared equation, but the returned axes gather
every original occurrence. Scalar, ragged, zero, and negative grids remain
invalid. 

At each grid point the angular frequency used in $D(\omega)$ and
$Y_{\mathrm{circ}}(\omega)$ is $\omega=2\pi f$ after coherent-SI conversion.

At every requested point SCNSim must form finite selected-network Y, Z, and S.
A failed Schur complement, source-boundary solve, Y-to-Z solve, or Y-to-S solve
fails the whole request as `DirectResponseFormationError` with the exact stage.
It publishes no partial grid, pseudoinverse, infinity, or stale family. For
every required $AX=B$, including multiple right-hand
sides, native Julia computes the normalized backward residual

$$
\eta(A,X,B)=
\frac{\lVert AX-B\rVert_\infty}
{\lVert\lvert A\rvert\lvert X\rvert+\lvert B\rvert\rVert_\infty},
$$

where absolute values are entrywise complex magnitudes and the matrix infinity
norm is the maximum absolute row sum. Exact `0/0` is zero; a zero denominator
with nonzero numerator is infinity. All operands and the resulting residual
must be finite, and

$$
\eta(A,X,B)\le\tau(n),\qquad
\tau(n)=256(n+1)\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{Float64}}.
$$

Here $n$ is the order of the square $A$ being checked. An empty complement that
requires no solve is a no-op rather than a zero-dimensional factorization.
The residual is a mandatory execution-time Gate. Native Julia does not expose
its raw value as a public Result or receipt field. Current JAX uses the
backend-scoped maxabs normalizer and selected real-dtype epsilon described in
Numerical arithmetic and diagnostic storage below; recorded quantity
certificates remain numerical evidence. Condition number is neither a Gate nor
a required computation.
The exact-open one-Port identity $Y=0,\ S=+1$ remains an internal algebra probe;
because finite Z does not exist, it cannot become a successful complete public
`DirectSolveResult`.

### Typed Direct quantity catalog

`run.evaluate()` evaluates one declared Direct physical quantity or
materializes the full dynamic operator without requiring an unrelated response
sweep:

```python
readout_root = DiagonalRootSpec(
    coordinate="readout_node",
    root_hint=6.0 * u.GHz,
)

evaluated = run.evaluate(quantity_view, readout_root)

evaluated.root
evaluated.frequency
evaluated.linewidth
evaluated.slope
```

For a named coordinate $r$ in the final View basis, this request solves the defining complex
root problem

$$
\left[\mathbf D_R^{E\downarrow}(\widetilde\Omega_r)\right]_{rr}=0.
$$

The selected Ref determines what this diagonal means. A final View may retain
one or several authored coordinates, eliminating only its complement with
`I_external = 0`; logical-Port loads and
other uncompensated stamps remain in the effective operator. The resulting
root is therefore loaded when those attachments are present. It is not the
uncoupled LC formula, a minimum or dip read from S, or a hybridized pole of a
larger retained block.

Required `root_hint` is a Quantity-valued approximate location used only to
start deterministic complex Newton for one locally simple, machine-resolved
root at the sealed baseline ParameterSet. It is not
the returned root, an optimization target, a constraint, or an implicit search
window. The evaluated frequency may differ from the hint. A non-baseline
ParameterSet, including every optimization candidate, uses deterministic
continuation owned by the identified baseline root; it never selects whichever
root is then closest to the original hint or to the preceding CMA-ES candidate.
Missing or dimensionally invalid hints and detected repeated or
non-continuable roots fail closed.

The selected-element root does not require positive-definite complete
capacitance. Its eliminated block must instead admit the checked solves used
to form the selected View operator and derivative at every Newton point.
Descriptor/infinite-mode interpretation beyond a locally simple root remains
outside this scope. The exact selected Schur element, analytic derivative,
32-update complex-Newton
limit, machine-resolution certificate, and deterministic dyadic continuation
are fixed in
[Diagonal-Root Numerical Procedure](implementation/diagonal-root-numerical-procedure.qmd).
V1 does not enumerate the complete QEP spectrum to certify this root.
Its certificate is machine-resolution evidence, not a validated global root or
analytic-branch enclosure; possible undetected Newton-basin exchange remains a
known V1 limitation.

`readout_root.frequency` on the Spec is an immutable selector that can be
placed in an objective; `evaluated.frequency` is the resulting Quantity. Merely
accessing the selector does not execute or consult process memory.

The V1 catalog is intentionally small:

| Spec | Declared operation | Public result |
|---|---|---|
| `DiagonalRootSpec` | Complex root of one named diagonal of the selected Direct dynamic operator | root, frequency, linewidth, slope |
| `OperatorElementRootSpec` | Complex root of one named row/column element of the complete final View operator | root, real-part frequency, slope |
| `HybridizedPoleSpec` | Complex root of the determinant of the terminal View's complete ordered retained block (at least two coordinates) | pole/root bundle with branch evidence |
| `TransferZeroSpec` | Complex zero of one ordered S/Y/Z input/output projection whose transfer denominator is finite and nonsingular at the candidate | zero bundle with numerator/denominator evidence; never a sweep minimum or implicit pole-zero cancellation |
| `ResidueNormalizedCouplingSpec` | Coupling from two selected machine-resolved branches with local slope/residue evidence and either one declared positive real frequency or the exact per-candidate `"complex_root_midpoint"` | complex coupling, its real/imaginary/magnitude projections, and the complex evaluation location |
| `ResponseElementSpec` | One S/Y/Z element at a declared frequency and ordered input/output coordinates | complex scalar and applicable real/imaginary/magnitude selectors |
| `OperatorSpec` | Full Direct dynamic operator on a declared grid | coordinate- and unit-bearing matrix Result |

```python
transmission = ResponseElementSpec(
    family="S",
    input_coordinate="feedline_in",
    output_coordinate="feedline_out",
    frequency=6.2 * u.GHz,
)

transfer_zero = TransferZeroSpec(
    anchor=6.5 * u.GHz,
    family="Y",
    input_coordinate=feedline_out_node,
    output_coordinate=filter_open_tail,
)

operator = run.evaluate(
    quantity_view,
    OperatorSpec(frequencies=frequency_grid),
)
```

Root-like bundles expose only physically defined typed scalar selectors such as
`.frequency`, `.linewidth`, `.magnitude`, `.real`, and `.imag`. For
`ResidueNormalizedCouplingSpec`, `.real`, `.imag`, and `.magnitude` are
nonexecuting selectors of the same complete complex coupling; Pint
`Quantity.magnitude` remains the numeric payload of an evaluated Quantity and
`abs(quantity)` remains ordinary Quantity arithmetic. Its `frequency` is
required and is either a positive real frequency Quantity or the exact literal
`"complex_root_midpoint"`; no other string, callable, manual complex frequency,
or implicit default is accepted. The midpoint is recomputed for every
candidate as `(omega_a + omega_b) / 2` from the complete complex branch roots
on the selected View. Each branch slope remains evaluated at its own root.
Their branch,
branch locator (including `DiagonalRootSpec.root_hint`), continuation,
local slope/residue evidence, units, ParameterSet, selected Ref boundary, and
operator identity remain attached. `DiagonalRootSpec` promises the documented
machine-resolved Newton procedure, not a globally unique spectral root. A
locally repeated/non-simple pole or zero, or a coupling input without its
required local slope/residue evidence, fails closed under that quantity's own
contract.
`HybridizedPoleSpec.coordinates` must equal the terminal View's retained
coordinate sequence exactly; it cannot introduce a hidden second retain
boundary. A real hybrid/zero anchor initializes a real angular frequency, while
a complex anchor preserves both declared components under the $2\pi$
conversion. An anchor is a Newton-basin initializer, never a nearest-root
instruction.

`frequencyAnchor` keeps that distinction in the exact request bytes. A plain
real Quantity encodes as `quantity_f64`; a Python complex Quantity, including
one whose imaginary component is exactly `0`, encodes as
`complex_quantity_f64` with independently canonical real and imaginary SI
bits. Both forms retain the declared source-unit provenance in the receipt.
There is no lossy real fallback, compatibility alias, or implicit removal of a
zero imaginary component.
`TransferZeroSpec` currently exposes only an ordered S/Y/Z projection; a
generic cofactor/minor object is not part of the V1 scaffold. The Spec also
requires its selected transfer denominator to
remain finite and nonsingular at the zero. A coincident numerator zero and pole
is rejected as an unresolved cancellation rather than published as a transfer
zero.
`RootSearchSpec` is an optional `search` declaration on the existing root
Specs. `method` and exact-tie choice `tie="unavailable"|"source_order"` are
required. The caller supplies exactly one real region as
`real_frequency_interval=(lower, upper)` or `hint_frequency_factor=<factor>`.
An optional `imag_frequency_interval` supplies two real frequency endpoints;
`None` adds no imaginary selection cutoff and is omitted from canonical bytes,
not represented by an infinite physical token.

A caller-declared "within ten times Hint" domain is expressed explicitly as
`RootSearchSpec(method="polynomial_transfer_zero", hint_frequency_factor=10,
tie="unavailable")`. For an original authored positive-real Hint/anchor $h$
and caller factor $k$, the positive RF real-frequency upper bound is $k h$.
A baseline or tracked branch anchor $a$ is a separate seed, not a replacement
for the original declaration $h$. No $h/k$ lower cutoff or imaginary envelope
is inferred. The captured factor is resolved against $h$, never the changing
tracked anchor $a$, so tracking cannot enlarge the declared region.

`method="polynomial_transfer_zero"` accepts no caller seeds. It applies only to
the supported intrinsic/non-Port Z transfer model with fixed mesh, declared
pure-inductive sections, static K/C/G and actual endpoint loads/View. The
same assembly coefficient authority forms the `2*n+1` Rosenbrock transfer-zero
pencil with the actual input/output, rather than treating pole eigenvalues as
transfer zeros. Candidates still require the original certified corrector.
Unsupported model capability fails explicitly. `method="finite_seeds"` requires
ordered nonempty caller complex-frequency seeds; it is an explicitly selected
alternative, never an automatic fallback. No sampling grid, epsilon,
deduplication, multiplier or smoothing is invented.

Omitting search preserves Hint/anchor-as-seed canonical fields. Every actual
corrected candidate or failure keeps its ordinal. A certified root outside the
caller region remains certified with an outside-selection fact, not a rewritten
numerical failure. Selection uses nearest-Hint complex-frequency Euclidean
distance and the caller's exact tie choice. No eligible certified candidate
means "not found from the declared trials", not "no root exists"; neither
method guarantees every physical root or global spectral uniqueness.
Discovery runs only at the initial requested point or optimizer original-point
anchor. Later points track the selected branch without rediscovery or
completion-order anchor updates. Implicit AD is local to the selected root,
not the discrete candidate sort. A same-point Objective may consume the actual completed root
packets together with their original selected checked Error archive. Its native
callable still rebuilds candidate(theta) and uses the local implicit rule, so
View/material coefficient derivatives are not frozen. Packets and Errors remain
runtime operands, never static cached values. The distinct completed Objective
variant key binds shape/dtype and the owned Error PyTree metadata, excluding
physical point and loss coefficient values. Compile-only warmup lists this
consumer as lazy until the actual producer tree is known; it does not solve a
root or claim that a normal raw variant warmed the completed consumer.
The caller can use region extent when authoring mesh resolution. Recording
search extent and mesh strategy does not automatically remesh a sealed Plan
or override its declared resolution. Explicit fixed meshes retain their
limitations without a new adequacy Gate.

`PreparedFunction` raw callables remain array-only local branch controls. Their
metadata records the declared search scope, but raw external AD does not run
high-level discovery/selection or acquire its certification. The high-level
corrector's actual selected packet carries the same candidate/program/View/
mesh/dtype and implicit equation derivative; it is not a frozen-root derivative
or a closure over Run, Result or executable ownership.

For the dev32 CONVERGING Z-transfer candidate, only the primal Newton update
residual changes to `r = cof_ji(F_eff)` for the actual ordered Z projection,
where `F_eff = (-i * omega) * Y` uses the same checked family state. Intrinsic
non-Port projections reuse its already checked selected `F/Fp`. Port
projections use the actual `Y/Yp`, with
`F_eff_prime = (-i) * Y + (-i * omega) * Yp`. The scaled represented
cofactor/determinant value and frequency-prime exponent ratio control the
update; no independent assembly, alternate loading or second transfer solve is
introduced. Nonzero omega is this mathematical representation's domain, not a
new frequency cutoff or search envelope.

Original cofactor(Y), full Z value/slope, denominator/rank, correction and
closure checks remain the success authority. The existing 32-step limit,
stagnation, failure stages and unexpected-fatal responsibility remain intact.
Y and S transfer update equations are unchanged. Implicit derivatives retain
the existing cofactor equation at a certified nonzero root; Newton iteration
history is not differentiated. The successor has a distinct numerical
algorithm identity, without a retained old/new execution switch or implied
bitwise trajectory continuity. Explicit caller-region candidate localization
and selection are a separate scope, not supplied by this residual change.

For the canonical `exp(-i * Omega * t)` convention, `.root` is the complex
angular-frequency Quantity, `.frequency` is `real(Omega) / (2 * pi)`, and the
positive passive linewidth is `-2 * imag(Omega) / (2 * pi)`. The Result records
the convention instead of inferring a sign from a plotted trace.

`QuantitySelector.on(view)` immutably and non-executingly binds one scalar
projection to an existing `NetworkViewRef`. A `CostObjective` accepts a closed
ordered expression of selector leaves, `QuantitySum`, binary `-`, and Python
`abs(...)`; it is not a standalone `run.evaluate()` request or a Python
callback. Every operand must have the same dimensionality, but leaves may bind
different Views belonging to the same captured Plan. No constants,
multiplication, division, or other general expression nodes are accepted. A
consumer may still request `OperatorSpec` and use
its labeled Quantity matrix for ordinary Python/NumPy calculation; a full
operator or matrix cannot itself become one scalar cost.

The fixed local numerical procedures, analytic derivatives, branch evidence,
principal-square-root convention, continuation, artifact units, and typed
failure mapping for this catalog are defined in
[Direct Poles, Zeros, Couplings, and Operators](implementation/direct-poles-zeros-and-operators.qmd).
That page implements this catalog; it does not add a second public selector or
global root-search promise.

The reusable definitions remain canonical in SCQ_Design:
[anchored diagonal roots and hybridized poles](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/numerical-methods/schur-complement-kron-reduction.qmd#anchored-bare-diagonal-roots-and-hybridized-poles),
[poles, zeros, and residues](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/network-modeling/poles-zeros-residues.qmd),
and the
[local residue-normalized coupling](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/network-modeling/poles-zeros-residues.qmd#local-residue-normalized-open-coupling).
SCNSim documents only how those quantities are selected, evaluated, and
evidenced.

## Optimization and numerical scaling

The dev27 CONVERGING preparation/display and resource-owner boundary is documented in
[Execution backends](implementation/benchmark-and-backends.qmd#warm-preparation-progress-and-evidence-residency).
`CircuitRun.warmup(view, spec, *, parameters=None)` prepares JAX signatures and
returns immutable preparation facts without numerical execution or stored
success. Its preparation-only path lowers exact shape/dtype signatures without executing
assembly, a sparse solve, Newton or a trial optimizer evaluation. The summary
identifies raw `PreparedFunction` transforms separately from high-level candidate
and frequency-chunk variants. Only an identical producer key and signature can
be reported as a later warm hit; aggregate compilation is not evidence of chunk
reuse. Explicit transforms and batch shapes are compiled as declared; unknown
sparse/implicit derivative shapes and future stage shapes remain lazy. The warm
holder follows actual device, canonical structural identity, dtype and fixed
capability partition. Static transformable programs and prepared handles use
bounded owner-local admission and active pins. Transient point operands, tapes,
factors and Results stay operation-owned. AD transforms the original callable,
never an AOT executable. `optimize(progress=True)` adds a transient observer distinct from the
durable callback; it cannot change numeric request identity or commit policy.
Display failures warn and disable display, while durable callback failures keep
their existing error contract. Private uncommitted-generation scratch is not a
checkpoint or a compatibility reader; current Workspace uses store revision 8 and evidence v3.
Intermediate continuation-step preparation and executable references end after
the synchronized result is observed, before recursion. The current stage owns
its fixed-model physical program and prepared variants; call-local frames,
factors, outcomes and ready-batch packets end after ordered consumption.
Candidate caches keep lightweight spool references rather than numerical
frames or full histories. Only bounded static programs and prepared handles
belong to the Run compile owner; unmatched transient operation state remains
operation-owned. Static shape changes between declared models may incur
recompilation. Native allocator or mapped-memory retention differs from live
owner references; releasing references does not guarantee immediate RSS return.
API wall time, inclusive phase/CPU costs and owner-held bytes retain their
separate measurement meanings, with no RSS or speed Gate.
The transient `population_evaluating` phase precedes ask and is not a durable
generation notification.

### Quantity objectives and backend execution ownership

V1 optimization evaluates Direct objectives only. It accepts any number of
same-Plan bound `NetworkViewRef` leaves, optimization variables, and scalar
quantity objectives:

```text
Definitions author
  ParameterSpec + immutable baseline + independent ref

Component Library author
  physical bindings + explicit public exposure + fan-out/AffineMap support

Circuit-model author
  reusable default OptimizationSpec + variables/bounds/objectives/optimizer

Notebook consumer
  inspect the default + provide a Design Target + optional immutable override
```

The following dev3/dev5 restrictions describe historical slices, not the current
physical-program capability boundary. Those slices changed executable selectors,
not the View model. `1.0.0.dev3` evaluated
`DiagonalRootSpec.frequency` and `.linewidth` on a supported retained quantity
View. Its original one-Port/no-trace restriction belongs only to that slice's
`solve_direct` response surface. `1.0.0.dev5` reuses the same CMA replay,
ledger, cache, retry, and winner contract while enabling
`HybridizedPoleSpec.frequency`/`.linewidth`, `TransferZeroSpec.frequency`,
`ResidueNormalizedCouplingSpec.real`/`.imag`/`.magnitude`, and
`ResponseElementSpec.magnitude`/`.real`/`.imag`. Before its historical owning slice, each selector failed fast with
`ScaffoldUnavailableError`. Current checked Quantity expressions are shared by
Sensitivity and CostObjective declarations under the physical-program contract.

`ParameterSpec` never owns optimization bounds. A circuit-model package may
instead expose one clearly named model default:

```python
def build_default_optimization_spec(target) -> OptimizationSpec:
    return OptimizationSpec(
        variables=(
            OptimizationVariable(
                parameter=model.shared_short_length,
                bounds=(0.6 * u.mm, 1.2 * u.mm),
            ),
            OptimizationVariable(
                parameter=model.idc_finger_length,
                bounds=(40.0 * u.um, 68.0 * u.um),
            ),
        ),
        objectives=build_objectives(target),
        optimizer=CMAESSpec(seed=17, max_evaluations=400),
    )
```

The consumer discovers the recipe without reading its source:

```python
default_spec = model.build_default_optimization_spec(target)

model.idc_finger_length.show()
default_spec.show()
default_spec.variable(model.idc_finger_length).bounds
run.explain(optimization_view, default_spec).show()
```

These surfaces answer different questions. `parameter.show()` reports the
independent definition's baseline and schema, not global Plan consumers;
`default_spec.show()` reports active variables, default bounds, quantity
objectives, weights, expanded normalization, and optimizer;
`run.explain()` reports Plan-specific consumers, maps, support, and the fully
bound request that would execute. None starts
a solver or writes the workspace.

```python
from scnsim import ParameterDefinitions, ParameterSpec

inputs = ParameterDefinitions(id="optimization_inputs")
resonator_capacitance = inputs.parameter(
    id="capacitance", baseline=110.0 * u.fF, spec=ParameterSpec(unit=u.fF)
)
```

This is a one-variable model-context excerpt. During the model's pre-seal
construction, pass `resonator_capacitance` to its real capacitor field and
register and wire that body in the model supplying `quantity_view` and
`readout_root`; creating this definition alone is not a physical binding.
Coupling stays a fixed Quantity, for example `0.12 * u.dimensionless`:
current `couple_inductive()` does not support parameter binding or
coupling-coefficient optimization. This supported capacitance-only example
does not claim that the earlier two-variable problem passed. Objective values
and weights remain illustrative requests, not achieved design claims.

```python
qubit_root = DiagonalRootSpec(
    coordinate="qubit.differential",
    root_hint=4.8 * u.GHz,
)

optimization_spec = OptimizationSpec(
    variables=(
        OptimizationVariable(
            parameter=resonator_capacitance,
            bounds=(80.0 * u.fF, 120.0 * u.fF),
        ),
    ),
    objectives=(
        CostObjective(
            id="readout_frequency",
            quantity=readout_root.frequency,
            target=6.2 * u.GHz,
            weight=100.0 * u.dimensionless,
        ),
        CostObjective(
            id="combined_linewidth",
            quantity=QuantitySum(
                qubit_root.linewidth,
                readout_root.linewidth,
            ),
            target=2.0 * u.MHz,
            weight=10.0 * u.dimensionless,
        ),
    ),
    optimizer=CMAESSpec(seed=17, max_evaluations=200),
)

optimization = run.optimize(quantity_view, optimization_spec)
```

The example uses the convenience form: `quantity_view` fills only selectors
that have not already been bound with `.on(view)`. Calling
`run.optimize(optimization_spec)` instead requires every leaf to be explicitly
bound. Normalization happens before request hashing; an unused convenience
default does not enter the request, and the two forms are identity-equivalent
when their effective leaf bindings match. All bound Views must belong to this
run and captured Plan or validation fails before numerical execution.

When objectives genuinely use different retained Views, bind each scalar leaf
instead of passing a default. In this excerpt, `qubit_view` and `readout_view`
are already-derived Views of the same `run` and captured Plan:

```python
cross_view_objective = CostObjective(
    id="combined_linewidth",
    quantity=QuantitySum(
        qubit_root.linewidth.on(qubit_view),
        readout_root.linewidth.on(readout_view),
    ),
    target=2.0 * u.MHz,
    weight=10.0 * u.dimensionless,
)
optimization = run.optimize(
    OptimizationSpec(
        variables=optimization_spec.variables,
        objectives=(cross_view_objective,),
        optimizer=optimization_spec.optimizer,
    )
)
```

Both Views receive the same candidate `ParameterSet`. This is not two searches
or a comparison between independently selected winners.

The best values remain an immutable `ParameterSet`. Reusing them is an
explicitly new request and never mutates the Plan baseline or the selected
Ref:

```python
winner_root = run.evaluate(
    quantity_view,
    readout_root,
    parameters=optimization.best.parameters,
)
winner_root.frequency
```

The model default is immutable. A consumer creates a `custom_spec` only when a
notebook must depart from it:

```python
custom_spec = default_spec.with_variable_overrides(
    bounds={
        model.idc_finger_length: (
            38.0 * u.um,
            76.0 * u.um,
        ),
    },
    allow_extrapolation=(model.idc_finger_length,),
)
```

Overrides use exact `ParameterRef` keys. `show()` distinguishes
`model_default`, `consumer_override`, and resolved bounds; the request owns all
three and its receipt binds them transitively through the request hash. There
is no global extrapolation switch or second hidden bound source.
Calling `with_variable_overrides()` never mutates its source: original
model-default bounds remain fixed, named overrides replace any prior override,
and unmentioned overrides are preserved. Its `allow_extrapolation=` argument
is the complete authorization set for the returned Spec rather than an
implicit union with the source. The full Spec, resolved bounds, and sorted
authorization identities enter request identity; only authoring-unit spelling
stays evidence-only.

Each `AffineMap.support` is a calibration-evidence interval. Values inside it
need no authorization. An out-of-support value fails by default; a request may
approve extrapolation only for named `ParameterRef` objects. An unapproved
optimization candidate becomes
`InvalidCandidatePhysicalParameter(stage="affine_support")` with tagged `Inf`
cost. Each actual JAX out-of-support fan-out records one evidence entry with the
public parameter, consumer edge, input value, support, side, and distance.
Its `authorization_sources` list retains each applicable source in order:
`parameter_set`, then `optimization_spec`; an unauthorized candidate has an
empty list. These are records of the executed request, not calibration of the
extrapolated region.
Distance uses the public input/support dimensionality and coherent-SI value
`support_lower - input_value` on the lower side or
`input_value - support_upper` on the upper side, and is strictly positive.
Binding order is fixed: resolve the public value, check every fan-out support,
validate authorization, apply each `AffineMap`, then validate mapped primitive
physical domains. Candidate ledgers own candidate extrapolation evidence;
ordinary solve/evaluate receipts own evidence authorized by their explicit
`ParameterSet`.

Read JAX Direct, Operator, and scalar Result records through
`result.evidence.get("affine_evidence", ())`. Each sweep `point.result` carries
its own occurrence's records, including repeated parameter points. This
read-only mapping remains available after Run close and Workspace resolve;
readback retains the original execution's authorization sources. If no edge
was outside support, the `affine_evidence` key is absent. Optimization candidate
records retain their corresponding conditional evidence in the candidate
history and objective components.

Authorization is request-local: passing an extrapolated winner to a later
solve/evaluate request requires a new explicit ParameterSet approval:

```python
approved_winner = ParameterSet(
    optimization.best.parameters.values,
    allow_extrapolation=(model.idc_finger_length,),
)

direct = run.solve(response_view, direct_spec, parameters=approved_winner)
```

The original winner values remain immutable; candidate and winner
`ParameterSet.allow_extrapolation` are empty. The new request records its own
authorization instead of inheriting the optimizer's approval.

Current JAX optimization uses the shared physical program and Python stage
controllers, with ordered ready waves and coordinator-owned publication.
In a Notebook, a DisplayHandle can update in place without polling:

```python
from IPython.display import display

handle = display("Optimization starting", display_id=True)

def show_progress(event: OptimizationProgress) -> None:
    handle.update(f"{event.phase}: {event.completed_generations}/{event.total_generations} generations; best={event.best_cost:.6g}")

result = run.optimize(view, optimization_spec, on_progress=show_progress)
```

`CMAESSpec` has the fixed public surface

```python
CMAESSpec(
    seed=0,
    max_evaluations=200,
    population_size=None,
    initial_sigma=0.25,
)
```

For $n$ active variables, `population_size=None` resolves to
$\lambda=4+\lfloor3\ln n\rfloor$. The sealed baseline must lie inside every
resolved finite bound or declared domain, maps to the initial optimizer mean $m_0$, is evaluated first, consumes one
evaluation, and remains winner-eligible. Baseline evaluation failure fails the
request. `initial_sigma` is a positive finite unit-coordinate scale. `seed`
accepts a signed 64-bit integer; an explicit population size is an integer of
at least two, and the evaluation budget must be large enough for the required
complete generation.

For every candidate, SCNSim binds its ParameterSet to the original Plan,
rebinds the shared physical program and its selected Ref operands, and
evaluates all objectives. A nominal reduced matrix is never reused across
different candidates. A singular/non-finite/branch failure is recorded as a
typed non-evaluable candidate, contributes `Inf` to the optimizer, and does not
publish stale or fallback quantities. Other candidates continue.

Optimization resume requires identical Plan, Ref, variables, quantity specs,
objectives, expanded normalization, algorithm, controls, seed, runtime, and
completed-generation ledger. An interrupted generation is discarded and
replayed deterministically rather than published as complete evidence.

For current JAX Optimization, the mandatory successful baseline and sealed
anchors remain pending in memory. There is no standalone baseline commit,
generation-0 checkpoint or initial progress callback. Only complete post-tell
generations count toward `commit_every_generations` (default 10). The first
completed generation batch includes the necessary baseline body once; generation
checkpointing additionally saves anchor restore state and the latest completed
post-tell CMA/RNG state, with generation at least 1. Checkpoint off omits
restore-only state. Workers install sealed anchors through an in-memory ACK,
without a storage transaction. Required group ACK precedes its one progress
callback; optional timing publication is separate and is not that prerequisite.
Error/interruption handling saves only the actual complete generation tail and
state. No failed or uncertain required batch is resent; the original error stays
primary. Baseline failure remains terminal and creates no checkpoint. Result
readback still includes the baseline and complete ordered numerical ledger.

The existing CMA request boundary requires a budget that fits the baseline
and at least one complete population. A budget too small for that population
is rejected; it is not a normal successful baseline-only optimization.
Interruption or failure before the first complete generation can retain actual
baseline evidence in its terminal record, without a generation-0 checkpoint,
restore anchors, barrier or generation notification. Failure handling does not
add a baseline-only protective flush or change candidate/CMA ordering.

An open linear domain maps
$x=x_0+s z$ with native full or one-sided CMA bounds; signed log domains map
$x=x_0\exp(z)$ with native unbounded coordinates. In both cases $z_0=0$ and
$x_0$ is the effective request Initial Parameters. The physical scale $s$ must
be finite, positive, and same-unit. `POSITIVE` and `NEGATIVE` require a strictly
signed nonzero $x_0$ and no physical scale; `NONNEGATIVE` and `NONPOSITIVE`
include zero but never relax model input legality. Mixed variables share one
request. SCNSim does not clip, mirror, use epsilon bounds, or apply another
physical transform. The request retains its declared seed, physical bounds,
coordinate scales and active-variable order. The Python stage controller drives
CMA through the shared JAX quantity evaluator.

### Engineer course realization {#ipf-optimization-example}

The Contract does not duplicate a complete workflow. The engineer course
teaches [Optimization](../examples/engineer/chapter-02/01-build.qmd),
[general RLGC](../examples/engineer/chapter-07/01-rlgc.qmd), and
[Direct analysis](../examples/engineer/chapter-04/01-physical-plan.qmd) as
separate native-API operations without becoming a second contract authority.

### Relative objective normalization

For `comparison="target"` (the default), every objective uses

$$
r_i = \frac{q_i-t_i}{s_i},
\qquad
J = \sum_i w_i |r_i|^2.
$$

For `comparison="at_least"`, its residual instead uses

$$
r_i = \max\!\left(0, \frac{t_i-q_i}{s_i}\right).
$$

An exact finite value equal to or above the target therefore contributes zero.
This is one-sided cost shaping, not maximization and not a hard feasibility
Gate. Every selector and internal expression node must remain finite before
comparison; failure or non-finite evidence cannot become a zero residual.

Normalization occurs before weighting, so `weight` expresses relative
importance rather than target magnitude or physical unit:

- for a nonzero target, omitted `scale` expands to `abs(target)`;
- for an exact zero dimensionless target, omitted `scale` expands to
  `1 * u.dimensionless`;
- for an exact zero dimensionful target, omitted `scale` fails closed; and
- an explicit positive, finite, same-dimensionality `scale` overrides those
  defaults.

SCNSim never divides by the current candidate `abs(q_i)`: that denominator is
undefined at zero and destroys optimization direction for a zero target. A
`CostObjective.weight` is required, positive, finite, and dimensionless. It
multiplies the squared residual as written above; it is not itself squared.
Explain/request/receipt surfaces store the expanded scale plus its source:
`relative_target`, `dimensionless_unity`, or `explicit`. These scales
nondimensionalize cost; they do not create a Gate, tolerance, or acceptance
rule. See the canonical
[normalized weighted objective](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/numerical-methods/auditable-scientific-optimization.qmd#normalized-weighted-objective).

### Four distinct scaling contracts

SCNSim keeps these operations separate:

| Operation | Purpose | May change |
|---|---|---|
| Unit canonicalization | Give a physical value one SI identity | Representation only |
| Optimizer coordinate scaling | Prevent raw unit magnitude from controlling search coordinates | Optimizer coordinates only |
| Objective residual normalization | Make declared metric errors comparable | Only Human/Design-Target-declared objective terms |
| Linear-algebra conditioning | Improve numerical solution of the same operator | Internal representation only; never physics |

Every active `ParameterRef` appears exactly once. Its lower and upper bounds are
finite, have the parameter's dimensionality, satisfy $x_{i,\min}<x_{i,\max}$,
and contain the sealed baseline in the closed interval. Linear variables are
converted to one coherent SI unit and mapped to dimensionless unit-interval
coordinates:

$$
z_i = \frac{x_i-x_{i,\min}}{x_{i,\max}-x_{i,\min}} \in [0,1].
$$

The default is this linear map. When a variable explicitly declares
`transform="log"`, its lower bound, upper bound, and baseline must all be
strictly positive. Using their positive coherent-SI magnitudes $\widehat x$,
SCNSim instead uses the dimensionless ratio map

$$
z_i=
\frac{\ln(\widehat x_i/\widehat x_{i,\min})}
{\ln(\widehat x_{i,\max}/\widehat x_{i,\min})},
\qquad
\widehat x_i=
\widehat x_{i,\min}
\left(\frac{\widehat x_{i,\max}}{\widehat x_{i,\min}}\right)^{z_i}.
$$

Taking a logarithm of a dimensionful Quantity directly is never permitted.
Invalid order, dimensionality, positivity, duplicate variables, or an
out-of-bounds baseline fails before an attempt. The ledger records both
dimensionless optimizer coordinates and physical Quantity values.

Objective targets and weights remain consumer/Human declarations. The product
rule above deterministically expands an omitted residual scale; unit conversion
cannot alter that scale, the target, the weight, a tolerance, or a Gate.

### Numerical arithmetic and diagnostic storage (dev22 CONVERGING)

Requested dtype, effective arithmetic and forward accuracy are distinct.
Compiler/View SI lowering remains binary64; selected JAX arithmetic uses
Float32/Complex64 or Float64/Complex128. A two-component expansion retains
low parts in that same base dtype and does not claim 128-bit accuracy or a
forward-error bound. Ordinary transpose, physical quantities, accepted
normalizers, tau and the 0.01 Hz complex Newton correction condition remain
unchanged; that correction condition is not a root-location error bound.

| Boundary | Rounding issue | Selected treatment and scope | Performance/evidence limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| SI lowering and dtype conversion | Information can round before execution | Binary64 physical lowering and selected-dtype conversion remain explicit | Compensation does not recover discarded input information |
| Indexed assembly/coalescing | Contributions can cancel | Existing narrow retained non-Port-realizable Z TransferZero high/low assembly | No universal speed or accuracy claim |
| Sparse high/low action and residual | Products/sums can lose low parts | Packaged C++17 CPU buffer kernel; ordered high traversal, low traversal, then combination; runtime CSR indices/coefficients/RHS | No dense operator or padded stencil; native buffer action is distinct from JAX executable compilation and requires no JAX CSR kernel download |
| Corrected Schur value/derivative | Subtraction can magnify rounding | One high factor and fixed primal/derivative correction; pair-aware residual and formation, then declared-dtype F/Fp→Y/Yp projection | Current cofactor/denominator consumes the projection, not an expanded output |
| Determinant and scale products | Intermediate overflow/underflow | Existing mantissa/exponent representation and family-specific normalization | Not a cancellation cure or confidence interval |
| Newton and certification | A derivative, correction and residual establish different facts | Existing analytic derivative, stops and typed failure ownership | No mean estimate, changed tolerance or automatic precision fallback |

The current JAX solve denominator uses maxabs of
`abs(A_hi+A_lo) @ abs(project(X)) + abs(project(B))` for the compensated
boundary. Backend-scoped norm definitions are preserved; maxabs is not a
matrix infinity row-sum norm.  Local physical inductor-block inverse preparation is distinct from
materializing a global network inverse. Numerical certificates and bindings
that a current quantity body records remain durable evidence; optional timing
is not copied into that numerical body.

`CircuitRun(..., timing="aggregate")` owns the diagnostic default.
Keyword-only `timing=None` on `solve`, `evaluate` and `optimize` inherits it;
explicit `"aggregate"` or `"detailed"` overrides it. Timing does not enter the
numerical request/cache/checkpoint mathematical identity and cannot force a
cache-hit recomputation. Optimization keeps generation-only clocks.

Aggregate mode keeps constant-sized phase accumulators within one operation,
attempt and clock, grouped by logical parent/dependency, backend/algorithm,
dtype/device and relevant shape/resource/cache condition. Frequency, point and
iteration remain context, not unique group keys. Each closed invocation is
counted once by status, with elapsed sum/min/max and deterministic max context;
a batch is one observation, never fabricated per-frequency durations. Mean is
read-derived. Incomplete intervals have no zero duration. Inclusive/nested
sums are not API wall time. Aggregates cannot reconstruct a detailed Timeline;
detailed mode stores actual diagnostic intervals only.

Operation SQLite evidence uses revision 8 and evidence version 3, with DELETE journal mode and EXTRA
synchronization. Verified object reuse is scoped to one transaction or readonly
snapshot, including hash/role/length bindings; a reopen or relock revalidates.
Manifest and operation start publish atomically; task/request/attempt/running
state and operation association register in one required transaction. Numerical
bodies are stored without occurrence context; ordered occurrences retain their
context and reference the shared body. Readers hydrate references in one
snapshot without executing a solver. Normal solve/evaluate commits result,
attempt success and first-success selection atomically, then publishes optional
timing and a separate final operation root. Older operation databases or file-journal
stores raise `UnsupportedEvidenceVersionError` with “use new Workspace and
recompute”; there is no legacy reader, migration, coexistence merge or automatic
delete.  Numerical commits,
checkpoint state, selection and callbacks retain required atomic ownership.
Timing batches publish separately with their own transaction identity/ACK,
reconcile uncertain outcomes without blind retry, and stop for that operation
on diagnostic write failure, including optional root finalization. Benchmark
status filters match recorded operation status or committed `task_status` and
preserve both independently; they never synthesize successful finalization
from task success. An otherwise committed numerical success returns
its result with `RuntimeWarning`; notification failure cannot mask the result
or primary error. KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit remain interruptions. Required
commit/integrity/worker/callback failures remain fatal as before.

### Linear algebra is not unit display

The small magnitude of an fF or nH value does not by itself prove that an
operator is ill-conditioned. Multiplying an entire equation by a scalar also
does not change its condition number.

SCNSim therefore does not expose a `ScalingSpec`, ScalingOptimizer, mutable
scale state, or automatic coordinate equilibration in Full V1.
Direct and Schur implementations must:

- use factorization/linear solves rather than a global network inverse; local
  physical inductor-block inverse preparation retains its declared algebra;
- compute and enforce every operation-specific normalized residual and
  machine-resolution certificate before publishing success; and
- keep those execution checks distinct from a Human-selected design-quality
  threshold.

Certificate durability is quantity-specific. JAX quantity bodies preserve
the explicitly recorded certificates and supplemental bindings. Optional timing
and unrecorded condition estimates are not numerical authorities. A verified
success binds the exact algorithm and semantic runtime source. `resolve()`
validates the durable chain without repeating numerical checks; a recorded
certificate is evidence of that execution, not a new forward-accuracy claim.

If later public fixtures demonstrate a real raw-SI conditioning problem, the
shared solve boundary may add a deterministic, reversible equilibration. Its
map and inverse must be recorded, and it must preserve the physical operator,
observables, and Notebook API. Such evidence would reopen only that numerical
implementation scope.

## Results, display, and reports

`Result` means an immutable value or fixed evidence selection. Inspection never
executes a solver; selected lazy access may perform bounded readonly evidence I/O. `AnalysisResult(Result)` is the receipt-backed terminal subset
returned by `solve()`, `evaluate()`, and `optimize()`. Every Analysis Result
exposes an immutable `ResultIdentity` containing its Plan, request, attempt, and
Result SHA-256 values. `DiagonalRootResult` is the concrete result of
`DiagonalRootSpec`; `resolve()` overloads preserve the corresponding concrete
type.

Completed JAX Optimization readback fixes its completion seal and minimal immutable
selection metadata. The generation Sequence and flat candidate discretization
use the selected indexes, verify bodies on demand and return detached values.
They do not preload every reference, replay all task history or capture the Run.
History, objective and parameter plots use bound summaries; comparison selects
baseline and exact best. Full iteration or slicing is caller-requested
materialization. The [lifecycle boundary](#package-lifecycle) owns the detailed
reader lifetime and missing/corrupt/replaced-evidence failure rules. Historical
files retain their execution identities; current revision-8 readers reject older
operation Workspaces, without migration or automatic destructive rebuilding.
Read-only Benchmark and checkpoint readers
retain their distinct responsibilities. Diagnostic batches advance their
published prefix only after a separate confirmed diagnostic acknowledgement.
Detailed mode preserves actual span/parent/clock facts; aggregate mode preserves
only the declared summaries. Diagnostic failure stops publication without
turning an unacknowledged tail into saved evidence.
These ownership changes do not alter numerical, ledger-order or winner meaning.

`ExplanationResult`, `CircuitDiagramResult`, and `ReportResult` are derived
Results. They do not fabricate request or receipt identity. `ReportSpec.inputs`
accepts explicit saved `AnalysisResult` objects or privately constructed
checked detached memory Results, including inputs from different Plans. A
report-only predicate verifies the actual typed consumer capability; saved
identity verification remains unchanged. Memory sources record ephemeral
Plan/request/execution provenance, never a fabricated saved identity. Each
source keeps its own provenance independently. Memory Direct/Operator matrices,
root/coupling summaries, Sweep outcomes, Sensitivity summaries and Optimization
history use the same pure composer, only where the materialized typed projection
supports that panel. No report access performs a numerical solve.

`ReportPanel` selects presentation from one exact object in
`ReportSpec.inputs`; an identity-equal replacement object is not that input.
Repeating the same Result object in `inputs` is ambiguous and fails; distinct
independently verified objects remain distinct even when their canonical
identities match.
The immutable panel is normalized once to one of `response`, `matrix`,
`summary`, `outcomes`, or `history`. It has no arbitrary keyword, callback,
layout, or execution surface. Omitting `kind` while supplying a family,
channel, case, or trace selector deterministically means `response`; an exact
frequency or matrix-style selector means `matrix`; and an objective,
parameter, or history selector means `history`. Conflicting selector groups or
fields that a normalized kind does not consume fail instead of being ignored.
Response channels resolve to exact `(coordinate, mode)` members, matrix
frequencies must be exact materialized points, and Optimization history
selectors must name objective or parameter evidence present in the completed
ledger. A parameter selector must also match the retained complete definition,
not only its definitions and parameter IDs. A failed HB case exposes no matrix:
report selection is limited to the case or to an exact declared trace/channel
pair captured from its verified request, and the report labels the requested
response unavailable alongside the typed outcome rather than manufacturing
values; a named trace includes its declared input and output coordinates and
modes.
`ReportSpec.panels` is optional and does not change the existing `inputs` and
`theme` meanings.

### Typed Quantity results

Result scalar and array physical values use the SCNSim Pint registry. Consumers
can convert presentation units without changing result identity:

```python
frequencies = direct.frequencies.to(u.GHz)
matrix_si = operator.at(6.2 * u.GHz).matrix.to_base_units()
matrix_values = matrix_si.magnitude
root_frequency = evaluated.frequency.to(u.GHz)
probe_loads = direct.y.view.probe_loads
```

Each `AnalysisResult` carries its exact Result/Ref identity for serialization
and audit; derived Results preserve their explicit source identities instead of
inventing an operation receipt. Every matrix view also carries the ordered
coordinate IDs, exact flattened input/output `(coordinate, mode)` channel
labels, and its per-probe `raw`/`compensated` load-state mapping. Direct uses
the empty mode tuple; HB uses coordinate-major/mode-minor channel order.
Passing typed Results is the normal downstream UX; raw receipt paths remain an
audit surface.

Result decoding detaches mutable mappings and numeric buffers once. Array
backing is immutable rather than merely marked `writeable=False`, so a normal
public attempt to re-enable writes cannot mutate verified evidence. Quantity
getters for matrix data, frequencies, scalar quantities, traces, operator
points, and HB states return fresh inexpensive wrappers/views over that private
backing, not a full matrix copy per read. Public Pint in-place conversion either
fails against immutable backing or changes only a returned wrapper. Lazy
parameter-point payload loading and artifact chunk reads remain lazy; this
ownership rule does not eagerly load a sweep.

### Display is explicit

Scalar `DirectQuantityResult.show()` returns an `HtmlPresentation`; its
`plot()` returns a detached Figure without displaying it. Other numeric
`result.show()` methods display one native Plotly Figure and return `None`, so
a final notebook expression does not trigger a duplicate MIME display. Their
`result.plot()` methods return the Figure without displaying it. Diagram and
HTML presentation objects retain their documented return behavior. Presentation
cannot execute, interpolate, or alter result identity.

`plot()` is not a universal Result method. Only a Result subtype with a natural
figure contract exposes it. Plot methods return the supported figure object so
the caller can display, save, or further configure it.

### HB case outcomes, traces, and display {#hb-cases-traces-and-display}

HB V1 is removed from 1.0. See the retained [HB V1 History](implementation/hb-realization-and-outcomes.qmd).

### Independent Direct and HB grids {#independent-direct-and-hb-grids}

HB V1 is removed from 1.0. See the retained [HB V1 History](implementation/hb-realization-and-outcomes.qmd).

### Explicit downstream sources

Reports name every source rather than selecting a latest result:

```python
direct_report = run.build_report(
    ReportSpec(inputs=(direct, evaluated), theme=Theme.AUTO)
)

report = run.build_report(
    ReportSpec(inputs=(direct, hb), theme=Theme.DARK)
)

selected = run.build_report(
    ReportSpec(
        inputs=(direct,),
        theme=Theme.LIGHT,
        panels=(
            ReportPanel(
                result=direct,
                family="S",
                input_channel="feedline_in",
                output_channel="feedline_out",
                magnitude="db",
            ),
        ),
    )
)
```

Report assembly records the exact chosen inputs and may combine a Direct
response with a typed quantity, include one complete HB batch and its declared
successful/failed case outcomes, or present one exact optimization result and
its candidate/failure evidence. An individual HB case is derived within its
batch and is not a separate `AnalysisResult`; using the batch preserves the one
terminal receipt. Report assembly never changes which candidate is best or
turns a Design Target into a pass/fail Gate.

When a Result has explicit panels, those panels replace its automatic figure
selection while its source-identity summary remains. Automatic report content
is deliberately conservative:

- a one-input/one-output Direct Result shows its named S magnitude in dB and a
  summary, without automatically adding phase;
- a multichannel Direct Result, scalar Evaluation, or Operator Result shows an
  inventory/summary rather than guessing a channel or expanding every matrix;
- a parameter sweep reads only point metadata (`parameters`, `source_index`,
  identity, status, and failure), never each point's lazy scientific Result;
  and
- an Optimization Result shows completed cost history plus its winner/outcome
  summary.

Standalone numeric `plot()` defaults remain unchanged. An explicit matrix
panel requires an exactly materialized frequency; a table retains the whole
complex, channel-ordered matrix, while a heatmap requires one explicit
component. An explicit HB response may select a declared trace or typed input
and output channels, never both. A named trace retains its declared input and
output Port/mode labels. `case=None` means all declared cases in declaration
order, with successful traces and typed failures visible; it never means the
first case. A failed selected case produces its outcome evidence rather than
reading an absent matrix.

`ReportResult.save(path)` accepts only a new `.html` path whose parent already
exists. It refuses overwrite, writes atomically, and returns a `Path`. The
single self-contained HTML embeds Plotly plots, summary tables, and every
source identity, but not complete large raw arrays, workspace links,
timestamps, or inferred PASS/FAIL claims. It bundles Plotly JavaScript once,
uses no CDN, and does not open a browser. User-derived labels and failure text
are escaped before entering the document.

`ReportResult.presentation_sha256` identifies the normalized input order,
panel selections, and resolved report theme. It is derived presentation
identity, not a calculation request, receipt, or authenticity signature.
Building a report cannot change any source Result identity or workspace state.

`ReportSpec.theme` accepts only `Theme.AUTO`, `Theme.LIGHT`, or `Theme.DARK`.
The report body, tables, and embedded Direct Figures share that one theme.
For numeric Figures, `AUTO` resolves to Plotly's configured template when each
Figure is built and does not track later browser/OS theme changes. Report
assembly resolves `AUTO` once from that same template and applies its paper,
text, grid, and first accent colors to the surrounding body and tables.
Omitted colors in a custom template use Plotly's ordinary light fallback;
unrecognized custom background syntax affects only the browser control-scheme
hint, not the resolved body color. Explicit themes stay fixed. Report HTML adds
no custom JavaScript solely for theme tracking; independent diagram SVG
behavior remains unchanged.

An invalid suffix raises `ValueError`, a missing parent raises
`FileNotFoundError`, and an existing target raises `FileExistsError`; other
filesystem failures remain their ordinary `OSError` subtype. Report export is
derived presentation and never creates an analysis attempt or receipt.

## Caller-declared schematics {#authoring-and-compiled-schematics}

Manual schematics are read-only Plan projections rather than reduced Refs,
solver Results or alternate topology authorities. The sole
[diagram contract](contracts/automatic-semantic-circuit-diagram-layout.qmd)
owns preparation, drawing units/body spans, complete caller geometry,
declaration/show ownership and actual-scene correspondence. Automatic compiled
drawing and the public representation selector are retired; mathematical
compilation and historical compiled exports are unaffected.

Preparation captures one immutable Plan/point inventory and measured contacts.
`render_schematic` requires complete layout and returns a detached certified
result. `declare_schematic` delegates that same render/certify/freeze and
atomically associates one completed drawing at its captured point with the
Plan. `show_schematic()` presents that already declared result; missing or
stale binding fails clearly without measurement, rerendering or solver work.
Layout units and spans are presentation-only, never physical TL parameters.

The authoring target's direct-connection surface is one N-endpoint
`link(endpoints=(...))` over eligible buses, taps, and pins. External grounding
has the separate `ground_pins(pins=(...))` operation; intrinsic branches retain
`scope.ground`, and logical Ports retain their own load/reference behavior.
Those forms share one final canonical reference without erasing owner-local
public boundaries or local diagram evidence.

The manual successor remains `CONVERGING` and under implementation. The
[central evidence status](contracts/index.qmd#implementation-evidence-status)
separates historical rendering evidence from this candidate. Superseded flat
authoring, catalog-hint and compiled automatic diagram producers have no
compatibility path.

The shared boundary remains narrow: schematic rendering does not seal or mutate
a Plan, execute an analysis, write a workspace, or change physical, request, or
Result identity. The target may project baseline values or one explicit
`ParameterSet`; it rejects `ParameterSpace`. PTC, retained coordinates,
transforms, selected Views, and numerical Results remain request/Result
evidence and must not be drawn as if they altered the authored circuit. Exact
point binding and `parameters_sha256` belong to the
[Parameter System Contract](contracts/parameter-system.qmd#parameterized-diagrams).

The two paths meet only at their shared exact Plan source and public references:
ASCDLS does not create, select, or mutate a `NetworkViewRef`, while
`CircuitRun` does not infer physical ownership or assembly intent from a View
or numerical Result.

All structured grammar, caller-declared manual geometry, native
Subsystem/Composite expansion, Port and ground projection, certified digests,
independent visible A/B reconstruction, separately verified source rows,
provenance, and diagram failure behavior belong only to the linked contract. A
successful current diagram certifies only its declared projection and exact
point, not a numerical calculation or whole-course acceptance.

The target failure boundary has two explicit stages. Missing/stale geometry,
wrong actual pin contact, missing required bodies/wires, broken conductive paths
and ambiguous electrical crossing incidence raise
`SCNSimValidationError(stage="schematic_layout")`. A mismatch between the
independently expected and reconstructed electrical or semantic manifest raises
`SCNSimValidationError(stage="schematic_audit")`. Either failure returns no
`CircuitDiagramResult` and allocates no runtime attempt, receipt, artifact, or
workspace entry. Text/body overlap and aesthetic spacing are caller-owned and
do not independently block a faithful drawing. No automatic avoidance or repair
substitutes for the complete caller layout.

## Failure and evidence contract

SCNSim-specific failures derive from `SCNSimError` through exactly five categories:
`SCNSimValidationError`, `SCNSimStateError`, `SCNSimCapabilityError`,
`SCNSimExecutionError`, and `SCNSimEvidenceError`. Every typed failure exposes
a stable machine `kind`, an exact `stage`, and immutable evidence. A started
operation seals its typed failure receipt before raising; preflight validation
creates no attempt. `resolve()` reconstructs the typed failure boundary but,
without a verified success, raises `ResultUnavailableError` and never retries.
Runtime preparation precedes request/attempt mutation; its failure raises
`RuntimePreparationError` without an attempt and leaves any already Plan-bound
Run workspace intact. Once an attempt is allocated, child launch failure and
every later missing or invalid outcome are attempt-backed
`BackendProtocolError` failures with a sealed failure receipt. Allocation
reserves ordinal/staging only; a blocked bootstrap lets Python finalize one
truthful immutable `allocated` or `launched` attempt record before numerical
execution begins.

The current public scaffold machine-maps `PlanSealedError`,
`WorkspacePlanReplacedError`,
