`WorkspaceVersioningDowngradeForbidden`,
`WorkspaceCommitIndeterminateError`, `UnsupportedEvidenceVersionError`,
`UnsupportedRuntimePlatformError`, `PortRealizabilityError`,
`InvalidDiagonalRootHint`, `InvalidOptimizationSpec`,
`DirectResponseFormationError`, `InvalidCandidatePhysicalParameter`,
`CompilerInvariantError`,
`UnsupportedSingularCapacitanceForDiagonalRootV1`,
`EliminatedBlockSolveFailure`, `RootSlopeUnresolved`,
`NumericalResolutionUnresolved`, `HBCaseFailure`, `RuntimePreparationError`,
`BackendProtocolError`, `ResultUnavailableError`, `EvidenceIntegrityError`, and
`ScaffoldUnavailableError`. The last is reserved for explicitly deferred
surfaces; it cannot represent an attempted numerical failure.

Ordinary Python call-signature and filesystem errors retain their standard
exception types where the Contract says so; they are not backend failure
receipts disguised as SCNSim numerical errors.

SCNSim fails closed for:

- an attempted `versioned=True` to `versioned=False` workspace downgrade, a
  malformed versioned index, duplicate Plan-to-iteration mapping, or replaced
  workspace accessed through a stale Run/Result handle;
- a request directory whose canonical request differs from the sealed Plan,
  Ref, Spec, ParameterSet, runtime, or operation; a second writer for the same
  workspace; or an attempt that would overwrite prior evidence;
- any target authoring violation involving duplicate IDs, an ordinary
  two-terminal native body outside exactly one structure, a multiply consumed
  body, an internally incomplete independent body, unbound required native pins,
  foreign/hidden endpoints,
  invalid series/parallel/branch/N-link declarations, invalid `ground_pins()` use,
  public exposure, transitive same-scope bus conflicts, physical-terminal
  shorts, or root Port attachment, as enumerated by the
  [structured fail-closed contract](contracts/circuit-plan-assembly.qmd#assembly-failures);
- a non-positive physical leaf R/L/C/`L_J0`, negative `Cj`, invalid RLGC
  conductor/reference identity, matrix shape/order/units, inexact symmetry,
  invalid Maxwell sign/row sum, failed C/L Cholesky, negative G/R minimum
  eigenvalue, invalid AEDT Q2D primary blocks or conductor map, or
  non-positive/non-integer section count;
- a general-line declaration mismatch;
- an invalid Composite public/hidden identity, a wired `CoordinateRef`, invalid
  `AffineMap` units/support/baseline, or mapped nonphysical child value;
- a SQUID without shared junction parameters or a valid finite loop;
- mutual coupling across Plans, across non-inductive or unoriented branches,
  or with non-finite/dimensionful `k`, `abs(k) >= 1`, or a complete bound
  inductance matrix that is not reciprocal positive definite;
- an unsupported component expansion or missing linear realization;
- an incomplete/invalid Plan requested for schematic rendering, an invalid
  diagram representation/theme, a `schematic_layout` preflight failure, a
  `schematic_audit` actual-scene correspondence mismatch;
- a bare physical number, unknown unit, foreign registry, or dimensionality
  mismatch;
- a current-runtime `ParameterSet` containing unknown refs, non-finite values,
  or another Plan family;
- a parameter definition, binding, set, space, sweep selection, collection, or
  parameterized diagram that violates the
  [Parameter System failure boundary](contracts/parameter-system.qmd#parameter-system-failures);
- invalid Port roles, reference impedance, load mapping, or ambiguous physical
  coordinates;
- an unknown, duplicate, terminated, foreign, or unevidenced PTC `PortRef`;
- repeated PTC or PTC ordered after `transform_pair()` or `retain()`;
- an automatic pair transform with unknown, duplicate, Internal, identically
  selected, differently referenced, or inconsistently oriented Public nodes;
- incomplete or ambiguous capacitor-branch provenance, a non-finite or
  negative physical branch capacitance, a non-positive external-cut sum, or a
  nonreciprocal compiled capacitance operator outside the declared scope;
- a non-finite or singular pair transform, a non-real/non-symmetric/non-SPD
  physical or transformed reference matrix, or failed principal-root
  reconstruction;
- a generated-coordinate collision, rank-deficient retained Port map, or
  inconsistent derived `A_k`, `B_k`, `R_k`, principal `D_k`, `Q_k`, or
  selected/omitted projector evidence;
- a `transform_pair()` across Port-bound nodes with different PTC/load states;
- an unknown or duplicate pump axis, drive, case, or trace identity; a drive
  bound outside the request; a non-positive/non-finite axis frequency; or an
  incomplete request-global drive materialization;
- a non-integer drive/trace mode, tuple-rank/order mismatch, non-current or
  non-finite drive Quantity, complex DC coefficient, or unknown drive/trace
  coordinate;
- an independently declared negative-mode partner, inconsistent current
  orientation/injection map, or invalid Fourier-coefficient materialization;
- an invalid per-axis harmonic declaration, negative/non-integer
  `max_intermodulation_order`, retained-lattice exclusion of a declared
  drive/requested trace mode, or exact tuple-frequency collision;
- an empty, duplicate, unknown, or Internal retained-coordinate selector;
- a Direct `solve()` view with a non-Port-realizable final coordinate;
- a PTC Ref paired with any nonzero effective DC or AC drive without explicit
  `allow_driven_ptc=True`;
- a non-full-rank transform or singular/non-finite Schur partition;
- disagreement between Direct and HB Port node, reference impedance, load, or
  selected-channel mappings;
- a duplicate optimization variable/objective ID, foreign or hidden
  `ParameterRef`, invalid physical bounds/coordinate transform, or foreign
  quantity selector;
- conflicting model-default/consumer-override bounds, an unknown override key,
  an out-of-support bound/candidate without per-ParameterRef extrapolation
  authorization, or extrapolation authorization inherited by another request;
- a bundle, full matrix/operator, or dimensionally invalid composition used as
  one scalar objective;
- a target/selector dimensionality mismatch, non-positive/non-finite weight or
  explicit scale, or a zero dimensionful target without explicit scale;
- a missing, non-finite, non-positive, or dimensionally invalid
  `DiagonalRootSpec.root_hint` (`InvalidDiagonalRootHint`);
- a sealed `CircuitPlan` authoring mutation;
- an unsolved selected-View eliminated block
  (`EliminatedBlockSolveFailure`), an unresolved/non-simple element slope
  (`RootSlopeUnresolved`), or a complex-Newton machine certificate that does not
  close within 32 updates (`NumericalResolutionUnresolved`);
- deterministic diagonal-root continuation whose physical path, branch, or
  subdivision cannot be completed, reported with its typed non-continuable
  failure rather than a different root;
- a locally repeated/non-simple pole or zero, or a residue-coupling input
  without the local slope/residue evidence required by its quantity spec;
- a transfer-zero candidate with a non-finite or singular denominator, or an
  unresolved pole-zero cancellation;
- a missing or mismatched exact receipt during resolve;
- a missing or inconsistent per-case SCNSim-to-JosephsonCircuits source
  coefficient/conjugate-mode map;
- a selected matrix whose per-probe raw/compensated load-state labels do not
  match its lineage and stamps;
- an attempted reconciliation across unequal topology, PTC/load state,
  boundary, reference plane, reference matrix, frequency, or wave
  normalization;
- an optimization resume fingerprint, expanded-normalization identity, or
  completed-generation mismatch; or
- a corrupt request, receipt, or artifact hash.

V1 exposes no public timeout, JobRef, or cancellation object. A
`KeyboardInterrupt` retains the original failure while the operation drains
its owned work and records actual interrupted evidence. A later call to the same operation appends a new attempt;
`resolve()` does not continue or retry it.

Condition number is neither computed nor published by the V1 Direct/root
runtime. SCNSim does not invent conditioning thresholds, optimization Gates, search
envelopes, targets, weights, or acceptance conditions from backend defaults or
tests.

Diagram failure retains its own evidence surface and cannot become successful
numerical evidence or overwrite unrelated numerical success.

## Known V1 limits

- Component authoring is limited to the explicit built-in catalog and custom
  Library contract in [V1 Component Authoring](component-authoring.qmd); there
  is no string discovery, mutable global registry, generic resonator topology
  enum, or arbitrary composite-child injection.
- Q2D ingestion accepts one primary general N-conductor R/L/G/C extraction and
  freezes its coefficients across the circuit solve grid. Frequency-dependent
  interpolation/extrapolation is not included.
- Composite mapping is limited to identity fan-out and `AffineMap`; arbitrary
  callbacks, expression ASTs, and calibration-table interpolation are not
  included.
- Direct element roots require a locally simple machine-resolved selected-View
  scalar root and solvable eliminated block, but not full-C positive
  definiteness. Descriptor-mode interpretation and complete-QEP enumeration
  are not included. Deterministic dyadic continuation does not provide a
  validated global analytic-branch enclosure.
- Direct JJ/SQUID behavior is the declared zero-phase, zero-bias `L_J0`
  small-signal realization; arbitrary bias-point linearization is not included.
- Automatic `transform_pair()` is limited to the declared reciprocal lumped
  two-node capacitance scope. It is not universal modal diagonalization and
  V1 provides no manual-weight override through this API.
- Direct optimization accepts one selected Ref per request and no Python
  callable, general expression AST, or persistent Julia daemon.
- Quantization is not included.
- No compatibility alias exists for the legacy Workbench import or bare-float
  physical inputs.
- No implicit latest-result selector exists.
- V1 has no public timeout, JobRef, cancellation API, per-candidate observer,
  polling service, or persistent Julia daemon.
- Structured authoring, Plan-identity integration, and certified diagrams are
  one `CONVERGING` scope with an integrated implementation baseline, not
  Human acceptance of the contract defined in
  [Structured Circuit Authoring and Certified Diagrams](contracts/automatic-semantic-circuit-diagram-layout.qmd).
- V1 has no public linear-algebra scaling configuration.



## History: dev28 共用編譯規劃與 native CPU 補償 {#dev28-compilation-ownership}

此範圍維持 `CONVERGING`。既有公開 Plan/Run/View/Quantity、Sensitivity、
CMA/L-BFGS-B/Hybrid、Result 與 Benchmark 入口，以及 SQLite revision 8，保持不變。
本次候選使用 `1.0.0.dev28`；支援目標限定 Python3.12、Linux x86_64
（glibc>=2.28）與 macOS Apple ARM（>=12）。Windows、Intel Mac、Linux ARM、
Julia 數值修改與 schematic completion 不在本次範圍。

Warmup 與 execution 共用不可變 execution variant plan，使用同一 callable、
abstract operand signature、cache key 與 Run-local compile owner。Warmup 只
lower/compile，不隱藏執行 baseline、root、factorization、candidate 或保存
成功 Result。Optimization 的已宣告 CMA cost、local gradient、Hybrid stage
與 Sensitivity derivative 類型，各自列出真正需要的 variants；不預編譯
未請求組合。依賴實際 linearization frame 的 consumer，若沒有同一 producer
的 exact static tree，保持明列 lazy，不以相同 array shapes 冒稱已暖機。

固定 ordered operand modes、comparison、layout、wrt、dtype 與物理結構之內，
theta/omega/seed 與 objective target/scale/weight 是 runtime operands，不以
其數值製造新的 executable identity。Exact zero-target smooth-square mode
仍屬明確 static mode；保留既有 smooth-square cost 與 abs-at-zero unavailable
責任，不把兩種數學模式混成一個假零導數。依 baseline 解析的 scale 只能在
正常 execution 中取得，warmup 使用其 abstract signature，不能偷跑 baseline。

CompileOwner 以每個 `(kind,key)` 協調 single-flight，長編譯不持有 owner global
lock。等待者共享實際 item，並各自持有到同步／必要 pullback 完成；等待者取消
只移除自己的等待，factory failure/interrupt 必須喚醒其他等待者並保留原 cause。
clear 不讓尚未完成的 build 延遲重新 admission；不清除其他 Run 或全域 JAX cache。
既有 16 program/16 variant/known256MiB policy 保持，unknown bytes 不冒稱 RAM 上限。
Run.close 仍拒絕 active operation，不兼任 cancel；detached PreparedFunction 仍屬 caller。

補償 host kernel 以 C++17 CPython buffer API 打包，不依賴 NumPy C ABI、Pybind 或
Cython，不提供 Python fallback。保留高／低位表示、dtype、ordered accumulation、
fixed correction、residual/certificate 與 failure 語意。Linux/macOS 預建 wheel
讓 uv 使用者不需 compiler；Git/sdist 的 native source build 仍需合適 compiler。
Artifact 存在不等於平台實際執行完成，實際 wheel/phase/lifetime 觀察另行記錄。


## History: retired Julia replay, supervision and HB examples

<details>
<summary>Version-bound retired mechanisms</summary>

Native Optimization uses a Workspace-owned `scnsim.native_result_index` v1:
sealed compact generation summaries and qualified artifact/body locators are
published before immutable success selection. History plots read those summary
chunks; selected-generation or candidate access reads its exact native artifact.
The Julia numerical body and artifact schemas stay independent and unchanged.
Reader construction verifies fixed root metadata; subsequent short reads verify
the selected index/body, without a full-history scan or rebuilding a missing
index. A missing or corrupt index is an evidence error, not an automatic repair.

Every SCNSim-triggered Julia startup, including discovery/juliaup, version checks,
initialization, preflight, inspection and numerical execution, belongs to an
operation supervisor. Dependency discovery runs in its managed helper process.
The native Run operation owns one supervisor before runtime preparation and
lends it explicitly to preparation, compiler inspection and execution. The same
owner keeps it through callbacks, Result decoding and recorder finalization;
an immutable prepared runtime does not hide a live supervisor. Standalone native
preparation owns its own scope. JAX scopes allocate no native supervisor.
Installed dependencies are not patched globally. A separate Kernel-liveness pipe
preserves stdin protocol and does not leak its writer into descendants. UI/network
disconnection alone does not cancel a live Kernel. Kernel death triggers
termination and reaping of direct managed roots, owned process groups, and
identity- and lineage-verified descendants; leases remain until actual drain.
Children that stay in an owned process group remain within that boundary.
Linux monitoring uses its platform-specific ownership mechanism. macOS uses
supported kqueue/libproc interfaces, without `NOTE_TRACK`, `NOTE_TRACKERR` or
`NOTE_CHILD`. An unseen short-lived intermediate followed by a child escaping
the owned group cannot be universally attributed; exec may also disrupt the
original parent lineage. Process names, PID alone or age do not establish
ownership. This boundary remains CONVERGING. Runtime preparation or smoke CI
is narrower than a macOS Kernel-death observation and does not establish that
observation. The supervisor has no COMMIT/checkpoint or numerical publication
authority, is not a persistent daemon, and does not claim protection against
arbitrary OS/process-tree disruption. Handled interruption
cancels queued work and drains active work before cleanup; garbage collection is
not a safety mechanism for external processes or publication.

`run.inventory()` is a shared-lock, read-only inspection of the exact leaf
bound to that `CircuitRun`. A replaceable workspace lists only its active leaf;
a versioned Run lists only its own iteration, never sibling iterations. A
stale Run raises `WorkspacePlanReplacedError`. Requests are ordered by
`request_sha256`, attempt ordinals are numeric ascending, and request status is
`succeeded` when a verified success exists or otherwise the failure/interruption
state of the greatest finalized ordinal. A verified HB batch remains
`succeeded` even when every case is a numerical failure. Hidden staging is not
an attempt; an empty request, broken hash chain, or invalid finalized attempt
is `EvidenceIntegrityError` rather than an omitted row. Inventory never writes
evidence and does not establish a hidden current/latest selection for
`resolve()`, reports, or any other API.
Its separate immutable `maintenance` tuple is empty or contains the exact
classified retired-leaf cleanup still pending for that root; inventory never
performs the cleanup.

The Julia process emits validated optimization progress, exposed by the optional
`on_progress: Callable[[OptimizationProgress], object]` keyword on both
`run.optimize()` forms. The existing native CMA events use `initial`, `resume`,
`generation`, `complete` or `result_reuse`, with stage `main` and strategy
`cmaes`. They retain generation and evaluation telemetry; local iteration
counters are `None`. The shared immutable model's additional stage/local fields
are defined in the physical-program contract above, not invented native events.
The callback return is ignored. Its exception terminates the child and is
reported as callback failure, without discarding already-published evidence;
`KeyboardInterrupt` remains interruption. Progress is process-local telemetry,
not Plan, request, candidate, or Result identity, verified Result, durability
promise, or scientific Gate. The built-in native display therefore reports an
unknown durable generation count until verified terminal success publication;
its completed-generation telemetry is not a committed-generation count. V1 has no per-candidate observer, public JobRef,
or persistent daemon.

Julia package precompilation may reduce load and first-execution latency but
does not promise every specialization is already compiled. SCNSim adds no
special precompile workload until representative measurement shows startup is
material to this one-process boundary. See Julia's official
[execution-latency and precompilation guidance](https://docs.julialang.org/en/v1/manual/performance-tips/#Execution-latency,-package-loading-and-package-precompiling-time).

Native Julia retains its existing baseline/checkpoint protocol below. The
mandatory successful optimization baseline is durably checkpointed before
the first generation. The request-owned checkpoint preserves the exact
baseline candidate and continuation roots; a separate immutable publisher seal
binds its original launched attempt. Reuse avoids repeating baseline work but
consumes no logical evaluation and changes neither CMA-ES state nor ordering.
The verifier reconstructs the baseline point and normalized coordinates from
the sealed request, rejects every incomplete or failed baseline, and binds
root dependencies to their successful terms without recalculating projections.
The final Result must exactly reproduce the verified baseline and primary View
lineage. A later attempt that consumes recovery evidence binds the exact
checkpoint content/seal pair.
It is partial recovery evidence only: inventory may report it without a final
attempt, but `resolve()` still requires a verified success. Referenced missing,
corrupt, symlinked, or unsupported-version checkpoint evidence fails closed. A
typed baseline failure remains a terminal request failure and publishes no
checkpoint.

The following process boundary applies only to the frozen explicit Julia
reference CMA path: one optimization attempt launches one Julia process. Parameter binding,
candidate compilation, Ref-lineage replay, quantity evaluation, shared
factorization/root work, objective aggregation, and CMA-ES remain inside that
process. Python submits the sealed request and receives process-local progress
and the final receipt; V1 has no per-candidate IPC/callback or persistent Julia
daemon. Repeated quantity identities share dependency nodes within a candidate.

In a Notebook, a DisplayHandle can update in place without polling:

```python
from IPython.display import display

handle = display("Optimization starting", display_id=True)

def show_progress(event: OptimizationProgress) -> None:
    handle.update(f"{event.phase}: {event.completed_generations}/{event.total_generations} generations; best={event.best_cost:.6g}")

result = run.optimize(view, optimization_spec, on_progress=show_progress)
```

`CMAESSpec` has the fixed public surface

```python
CMAESSpec(
    seed=0,
    max_evaluations=200,
    population_size=None,
    initial_sigma=0.25,
)
```

For $n$ active variables, `population_size=None` resolves to
$\lambda=4+\lfloor3\ln n\rfloor$. The sealed baseline must lie inside every
resolved finite bound or declared domain, maps to the initial optimizer mean $m_0$, is evaluated first, consumes one
evaluation, and remains winner-eligible. Baseline evaluation failure fails the
request. `initial_sigma` is a positive finite unit-coordinate scale. `seed`
accepts a signed 64-bit integer; an explicit population size is an integer of
at least two, and the evaluation budget must be large enough for the required
complete generation.

The runtime pins
[CMAEvolutionStrategy.jl 0.2.6](https://github.com/jbrea/CMAEvolutionStrategy.jl/tree/v0.2.6),
registry tree `6bf0985be2c5ea58305d2d04e336684f64fdc12a`. Its public
`minimize()` initializes

$$
C_0=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\exp(10^{-4}i/n)\right),
\qquad i=0,\ldots,n-1,
$$

rather than exact identity. A finite-bounded variable retains the original
$z\in[0,1]$ coordinate and package lin-quad bounds. An open linear domain maps
$x=x_0+s z$ with native full or one-sided CMA bounds; signed log domains map
$x=x_0\exp(z)$ with native unbounded coordinates. In both cases $z_0=0$ and
$x_0$ is the effective request Initial Parameters. The physical scale $s$ must
be finite, positive, and same-unit. `POSITIVE` and `NEGATIVE` require a strictly
signed nonzero $x_0$ and no physical scale; `NONNEGATIVE` and `NONPOSITIVE`
include zero but never relax model input legality. Mixed variables share one
request. SCNSim does not clip, mirror, use epsilon bounds, or apply another
physical transform. The signed Int64 seed is
reinterpreted as UInt64 with the same bits. The canonical request carries the
Python-prepared baseline coordinates as
`baseline_optimizer_coordinates_f64` in variable order. Julia consumes these
exact IEEE-754 bits instead of recomputing the logarithmic normalization with
its system math library; candidate mapping and CMA sampling/update remain the
pinned Julia path.

The fixed request identities are
`algorithm_id="scnsim.direct_cmaes.cmaes_jl_0_2_6_state_replay.v9"` and
`box_transform_id="cmaes-jl-0.2.6-linquad-unit-box.v1"` for all-bounded
requests or `cmaes-jl-0.2.6-native-domains.v1` when any domain is present.
The call uses
`popsize=lambda`, `maxiter=g`, `maxfevals=nothing`,
`parallel_evaluation=true`, `multi_threading=false`, and `verbosity=0`, with
ftol, xtol, stagnation, target, time, and noise controls set to `nothing`. Its
internal callback captures evaluated-generation evidence and emits progress;
it does not change sampling or stopping, and ledger sealing waits for the
continuation boundary below. With
budget $B$, it runs exactly
$g=\lfloor(B-1)/\lambda\rfloor$ complete generations and requires $g\ge1$;
unused remainder is evidence. Candidate failures and cache hits still consume
their declared population ordinal. The winner is the lowest finite cost among
the baseline and completed candidates; an exact cost tie selects the earliest
evaluation ordinal in baseline, generation, then population-column order.
These execution controls bound reproducibility but do not decide whether the
result meets a Design Target.

A closed request envelope bound to an exact known v3 through v8 outer optimization
identity raises `UnsupportedEvidenceVersionError` with the operation and exact
expected/observed algorithm IDs. This identifies the need for its original
source-bound runtime; it does not claim the historical request's remaining
contents were verified. Malformed envelopes, wrong Plan/request bindings, and
current-version evidence corruption remain `EvidenceIntegrityError`.

Version 7 binds the closed scalar-expression tree, its exact per-node unit
conversion order, and target/at-least comparison semantics. It retains version
6's Python-owned baseline coordinate bits and the pinned CMA sampling/update
mathematics.

Version 9 additionally binds candidate-local complex-root-midpoint coupling
and the complete complex coupling witness retained by every successful coupling
term. Python checks its sealed request and evidence identities, not the
backend's midpoint or magnitude arithmetic. Version 8 remains a
known published predecessor and is rejected through the typed unsupported-
version path rather than being relabelled as current or corrupt evidence.

Every population outcome records both the callback-visible raw CMA sample
column `optimizer_latent_coordinates_f64` and its transformed optimizer
`optimizer_coordinates_f64` beside the physical bindings. Both arrays have
length $n$ in request-variable order. Retry invokes the
same pinned `minimize()` from the original seed. The batch objective verifies
the transformed coordinates, generation, and population column before
returning stored costs; the package callback then verifies the raw sample bits
before the mean or covariance update. The raw check is mandatory because the
bounded lin-quad transform is many-to-one. The first unsealed generation resumes
physical evaluation. SCNSim neither serializes nor restores the package's
private optimizer object; either replay mismatch is `EvidenceIntegrityError`.

A callback precedes the package update and therefore cannot by itself seal a
resumable generation. Each verified ledger also carries the canonical
`cmaes-jl-0.2.6-julia-1.12.6-continuation-state.v1` certificate over all
future-affecting mean, sigma/path, covariance/decomposition, stop, constraint,
and exact MersenneTwister fields. For $k<g$, ledger $k$ becomes verified only at
callback $k+1$ before its update, under boundary
`post_update_post_next_sample_pre_next_update`; the certificate also covers the
next raw and transformed `[n, lambda]` populations. Interruption before that
boundary falls back to ledger $k-1$. The final ledger is certified only after
`minimize()` returns under `terminal_post_update`, with `Stop.it=g` and
`reason=:maxiter`. For sealed generations retry compares transformed samples
before returning stored costs. For the first unsealed generation it caches the
transformed sample, evaluates normally, and compares package state, RNG, raw
sample, and cached transformed sample against the preceding certificate in the
callback before update or evidence publication. These hashes are
continuation-integrity evidence, not independently reconstructable state
artifacts, and are never restored as optimizer state.

For every candidate, generation-ledger version 3 stores each objective's bound
quantity plus one record for every leaf selector and View in request order.
Successful leaves carry their actual realized lineage and evaluated Quantity;
failures preserve already evaluated terms and mark the exact failed or
not-evaluated remainder. Successful objectives additionally store their
evaluated Quantity, signed normalized residual, and weighted component cost.
Optimization-owned failures carry a closed context that binds the logical
candidate position, execution phase, public `objective_id` plus one-based
`term_ordinal` where applicable, request-derived View/quantity dependency keys,
and the authored-order affected leaves. View realization affects only that
View's consumers; a dependency failure affects its triggering leaf and blocked
same-dependency consumers. A residue selector's two private branch roots retain
distinct dependency identities, and a failed branch names only public
selectors that consume that root. Projection-only failure affects its owner leaf; and
candidate preparation/compilation affects every leaf. Objective and total
aggregation retain completed term/component evidence without inventing a
failed leaf. The baseline uses ordinal/generation zero and null population
column, including `baseline_root_anchor` failures before a candidate record,
and every such baseline failure aborts the request.
For a terminal population failure, the generation is the next unsealed
generation after the verified ledger prefix and remains inside the requested
generation bound; its column is bounded by the requested population size and
must reproduce the public evaluation ordinal. This is position consistency,
not independent observation of the last live child column. Within a failed
objective, terms before the one failure are successful and later terms are
not evaluated; an objective-aggregation failure instead retains all of that
objective's terms as successful.
The request-owned target, resolved scale/source, and weight bind each
successful component and total in the sealed request and producer evidence;
Python checks typed finite, nonnegative successful costs but does not
recalculate expression, residual, weighted, or total-cost arithmetic. A
candidate-dependent invalid
primitive value is `InvalidCandidatePhysicalParameter`; eliminated-block,
local-slope, and Newton/continuation failures retain their corresponding typed
root errors and tagged positive-infinity penalty. If any of those occurs while
evaluating the mandatory baseline, the request fails instead of creating an
optimization Result. Invalid variables, bounds, objectives, selectors, or
controls fail preflight as `InvalidOptimizationSpec`; a compiler invariant,
runtime failure, or process protocol failure aborts the request rather than
becoming a candidate outcome.

For every candidate, SCNSim binds its ParameterSet to the original Plan,
compiles that candidate, replays the complete selected Ref lineage, and
evaluates all objectives. A nominal reduced matrix is never reused across
different candidates. A singular/non-finite/branch failure is recorded as a
typed non-evaluable candidate, contributes `Inf` to the optimizer, and does not
publish stale or fallback quantities. Other candidates continue.

Optimization resume requires identical Plan, Ref, variables, quantity specs,
objectives, expanded normalization, algorithm, controls, seed, runtime, and
completed-generation ledger. An interrupted generation is discarded and
replayed deterministically rather than published as complete evidence.

For current JAX Optimization, the mandatory successful baseline and sealed
anchors remain pending in memory. There is no standalone baseline commit,
generation-0 checkpoint or initial progress callback. Only complete post-tell
generations count toward `commit_every_generations` (default 10). The first
completed generation batch includes the necessary baseline body once; generation
checkpointing additionally saves anchor restore state and the latest completed
post-tell CMA/RNG state, with generation at least 1. Checkpoint off omits
restore-only state. Workers install sealed anchors through an in-memory ACK,
without a storage transaction. Required group ACK precedes its one progress
callback; optional timing publication is separate and is not that prerequisite.
Error/interruption handling saves only the actual complete generation tail and
state. No failed or uncertain required batch is resent; the original error stays
primary. Baseline failure remains terminal and creates no checkpoint. Result
readback still includes the baseline and complete ordered numerical ledger.

The existing CMA request boundary requires a budget that fits the baseline
and at least one complete population. A budget too small for that population
is rejected; it is not a normal successful baseline-only optimization.
Interruption or failure before the first complete generation can retain actual
baseline evidence in its terminal record, without a generation-0 checkpoint,
restore anchors, barrier or generation notification. Failure handling does not
add a baseline-only protective flush or change candidate/CMA ordering.



```python
direct = run.solve(feedline, DirectSolveSpec(...))
hb = run.solve(feedline, HBSolveSpec(...))
readout = run.evaluate(feedline, DiagonalRootSpec(...))
optimization = run.optimize(feedline, OptimizationSpec(...))
```

| How are HB drives, cases, mixing, truncation, traces, and displays expressed? | [Named HB drives, cases, mixing, and driven PTC](#named-hb-drives-cases-and-mixing) and [HB cases, traces, and display](#hb-cases-traces-and-display) |


| What are the named HB case responses? | `run.solve(ref, spec)` | `HBSolveSpec` | `HBBatchResult` with one typed outcome per declared case |


- an HB batch shows every declared case outcome, including typed failures;


- any zero-frequency HB linear-response input or output mode;


- an HB pair transform involving any non-Port-bound input node;


- an HB backend result that cannot bind complete mode-port Z, signed
  frequencies, input/output `W` normalization, phasor/mode-index conversion,
  or the required lifted operator identity;


- an HB adapter that reverses tuples and conjugates twice, cannot prove its
  same-signed-frequency permutation, or cannot de-embed every backend source
  resistor before selected-network construction;


- a returned HB case whose independently recomputed final residual satisfies
  neither fixed V1 condition, recorded as that case's `HBCaseFailure` rather
  than request success data;


- JosephsonCircuits flux-pump and three-wave-mixing behavior retains its
  upstream relatively-untested limitation.


- HB V1 uses one fixed, versioned numerical policy and independent zero-state
  initialization per case. It exposes no `HBNumericsSpec`, warm-start policy,
  multithreaded batch mode, or callback hook.


- HB reduction acts on the small-signal sideband operator after the original
  nonlinear balance; nonlinear model-order reduction is not included.


- Driven PTC is a compensated small-signal view around a static/nonlinear
  balance that still contains the selected shunts; it is not an unloaded
  operating-point solution.


- HB optimization objectives are not included; optimization is Direct-only.


- Direct and HB may use independent grids; comparison performs no implicit
  interpolation.


</details>


## History: retired HB-only declarations

<details>
<summary>Removed HB surface</summary>

Partial HB case failure and Direct/HB grid comparison have explicit contracts
below. The stabilized implementation does not leave either behavior to backend
or implementation convenience.

JosephsonCircuits is an HB backend. It is not the authority for SCNSim
topology, coordinate names, Direct operators, reductions, or public consumer
contracts.

The new HB request uses the explicitly selected `feedline` lineage plus the
winner ParameterSet. A ParameterSet never carries or changes a Ref lineage;
the optimization source remains parameter provenance.

Every HB Result additionally records the request-global pump-axis and drive
schemas; operating-point and modulation limits; optional intermodulation crop;
three-/four-wave-mixing selections; retained mode tuples, signed frequencies,
and mode-port order; solver normalization and version; input/output `W`
matrices; solver-to-SCNSim phasor, mode-index, and `returnZ`/`returnS`
conversion, same-signed-frequency permutation, and single-conjugation proof;
and the source-loaded, intrinsic, selected-network, and reconciliation
identities.
Each case records its declared current contributions, generated conjugates,
SCNSim-to-solver coefficient/index map, oriented injection maps, effective
mode-indexed source vectors, derived Bias/Pump states, and exact case identity.
A driven PTC Result also records
`allow_driven_ptc`, loaded balance topology, and compensated analysis topology.

HB may additionally expose backend-native and reconciliation evidence. Direct
does not acquire a fake case layer. S display accepts
`magnitude="linear" | "db"`; dimensionful Y/Z matrices remain linear Quantity
surfaces.

</details>
